If anyone sinned by not testifying about something he saw or heard, when he was required to testify, he becomes guilty of sinning.
What would one become who touched anything unclean?
If anyone touched any unclean thing, that person is unclean, and he will be guilty.
What must the one do who is guilty of sin?
The one who is guilty of sin must bring the required penalty for his guilt to Yahweh.
What animal should he bring to Yahweh for a sin offering?
He should bring to Yahweh a female goat or lamb.
If the individual cannot afford to buy a lamb or goat, what should he bring to Yahweh for the guilt offering?
If he cannot afford a lamb or goat, for the guilt offering he should bring two doves or two pigeons.
If he could not afford two doves or two pigeons, what could he bring for his sin offering?
If he could not afford two doves or two young pigeons for his restoring sacrifice, he could bring a tenth of an ephah of fine flour without any oil or incense on it.
What offering must be brought if anyone breaks a commandment and unintentionally desecrates the sacred space where Yahweh lives or the sacred items that are devoted to Yahweh?
This guilt offering must be a perfect ram from the flock.
What did one have to do if he sinned against his neighbor?

If a person sinned against his neighbor, on the day that he recognizes his guilt, he must restore whatever he took or the lost thing that he had found and add a fifth more value to what he restores or returns.
What must one do who swore falsely about any matter?
If one swore concerning something as a lie, he must restore the full value and add one-fifth of its value to it.
What should someone bring to the priest for a guilt offering if he is guilty of the sins above?
If one is guilty of the sins above, he must bring a purifying offering, a perfect ram from the flock.
How long must the burnt offering remain on the altar?
The burnt offering must remain burning on the altar all night, until the morning.
What must the priest wear to remove the fatty ash from the altar?
The priest must put on his linen robe and underclothes to remove the ashes from the altar.
What must the priest do before carrying the ashes outside the camp?
The priest had to take off his linen clothes and put on other clothes before taking the fatty ash outside of the camp.
What must be kept going at all times?
The fire on the altar must be made to burn on the alter; it must not go out.
What should the priests to do with the leftover unleavened bread?
In a holy place; in the courtyard of the tent of meeting, Aaron and his sons should eat the unleavened bread.
What do the sons of Aaron have to do when their sons are anointed?
The sons of Aaron must present a grain offering of a tenth part of an ephah of fine flour, half in the morning and half in the evening.
How must this grain offering be prepared?
This grain offering must be combined with oil and made on a griddle in oil.
Who would offer this grain offering?
The priest who is in line to succeed the current high priest should perform the grain offering in this way.
According to the law of the sin offering, what did the priest have to do to the offering?
The priest had to eat the sin offering in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
What had to be done with the clay pot in which the meat was boiled?
The clay pot in which the meat was boiled had to be shattered.
What part of the sin offering was not to be eaten?
No part of the sin offering was to be eaten from which blood was brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the holy place.
What offering was like the sin offering?
The guilt offering was like the sin offering.
What belongs to the priest from anyone’s burnt offering?
The skin of the burnt offering that anyone presents belongs to the priest who offers the offering.
Which offering belonged to the priests?
Every grain offering belonged to all the sons of Aaron.
By the third day, what must be done with the remaining meat of the sacrifice?
The meat of the sacrifice that remains uneaten must be burned on the third day.
What had to be done to anyone who is eating fat from an animal or blood from a bird or an animal?
Anyone who is eating fat from the livestock or blood from a bird or livestock must be cut off from his people.
What has to be given to the priest after the fat is burned on the altar and the breast is given to Aaron and for his sons?
After the fat is burned on the altar and the breast is given to Aaron and for his sons, the right thigh must be given to the priest who performs the sacrifice of your peace offerings.
What did Yahweh tell Moses to do with Aaron and his sons?
Yahweh told Moses to take Aaron and his sons, their special clothes and the anointing oil, the bull, two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread to the entrance to the tent of meeting.
Who did Yahweh tell Moses to call to the entrance of the tent of meeting?
Yahweh told Moses to assembly all the people at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
What clothing did Moses put on Aaron?
Moses put the embroidered tunic on Aaron, tied the waistband around him, and clothed him with the outer garment and the priests’ sacred apron.
What did Moses place on the breastplate?
Moses put the Urim and the Thummim on the breastplate.
What was the crown of holiness?
The holy crown was the golden flower-shaped plate fastened to the front of the turban.
What did Moses anoint with the anointing oil?
Moses anointed the sacred tent and everything in it with the anointing oil, making them holy.
Moses consecrated Aaron by pouring some of the oil of anointing on the head of Aaron.
What did Moses do with the blood of the bull that was brought for the sin offering?
Moses took the blood and put it on the horns of the altar with his finger. He then poured out the blood at the base of the altar.
What did Moses do with the blood from the ram used for the burnt offering?
Moses splashed its blood against every side of the altar.
What did Moses do with some of the blood from the second ram, the ram of consecration?
Moses took some of the blood from the ram of consecration and placed it on the lobe of Aaron’s right ear, the thumb of his right hand, and the big toe on his right foot.
How long were the priests to remain at the entrance to the tent of meeting?
The priests were to remain at the entrance to the tent of meeting for seven days and seven nights.
What was Aaron and his sons’ response to what Yahweh had ask them to do?
They did all the things God had commanded them through Moses.
On what day did Moses call to Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel?
Moses called to Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel on the eighth day.
What two animals did Moses ask Aaron and his sons to bring to offer to Yahweh?
Moses ask Aaron to take a calf from the bulls for a sin offering and a perfect ram for a burnt offering to Yahweh.
What animals did Moses ask Aaron to tell the people of Israel to bring to offer to Yahweh?
Moses asked Aaron to tell the people to bring a male goat, a calf, a lamb, an ox, and a ram to offer to Yahweh.
Why had Yahweh commanded them to do this?
Yahweh commanded them to do this and they would see how glorious Yahweh is.
After Aaron made the offerings as Moses had said, what did Aaron do for the people?
After Aaron made the offerings, he lifted up his hands toward the people and he blessed them.
What happened when the glory of Yahweh appeared to the people?
When the glory of Yahweh appeared to the people, fire went forth before the face of Yahweh and consumed the burnt offering and fat on the altar.
What did the people do when the fire came from Yahweh?
When the fire came out from Yahweh, the people shouted and fell on their faces.
Who offered unacceptable fire to Yahweh?
Nadab and Abihu, sons of Aaron, offered strange fire to Yahweh that he did not command them.
What happened to these two men as a result of this act?
Fire shot out from Yahweh and consumed them. They died in Yahweh’s presence.
Who was called upon by Moses to carry the bodies out of the tabernacle?
Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, the uncle of Aaron, were called by Moses to carry the corpses outside the camp.
What did Moses say to Aaron and his sons?
Moses said to them that they should not go out of the tent of meeting or they would die.
What did Yahweh say to Aaron and his sons about what they should not drink?
Yahweh told Aaron and his sons that they should not drink wine or beer before entering the tent of meeting.
Why was Moses angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, the remaining sons of Aaron?
Moses was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar because they had let the goat for the sin offering burn up instead of eating it.
What living things that live on the earth did Yahweh tell Moses and Aaron the people of Israel could eat?
Yahweh told Moses and Aaron to tell the people of Israel they could eat any livestock that completely cloven hooves and rechews partially digested food.
Was an animal acceptable to eat if it only had a split hoof or if it only chewed the cud?
If an animal possessed only one of the two traits, it was not acceptable to eat.
What animals living in the water may be eaten by the people of Israel?
The people of Israel may eat anything that lives in the water and has both fins and scales.
What kind of birds did Yahweh say the people of Israel should detest and not eat?
Yahweh said that the people of Israel should detest and not eat eagles, falcons, hawks, vultures and ravens, owls ostriches and even bats.
What kinds of insects could be eaten by the people?
Insects that walk on legs above their feet, which they use to leap on the ground, may be eaten by the people.
What should the people do to four-legged insects that fly?
The people should consider any four-legged insect that swarms to be disgusting and completely unacceptable to eat.
What animals that swarm on the ground should the people of Israel consider to be unclean?
The weasel, the rat, every kind of large lizard, the gecko, the monitor lizard, the lizard, the skink, and the chameleon are unclean.
What happens to anything that an unclean animal touches?
Anything upon which the body of an unclean animal falls shall be unclean.
What does Yahweh say about things that crawl on the ground?
All the animals that crawl upon the ground on four or more legs are to be considered disgusting and unacceptable to eat.
Why did Yahweh say that the people of Israel must be holy?
Yahweh said that the people must be holy because he is holy.
What did Yahweh say to Moses about women who give birth to a male child?
Yahweh said to Moses that a woman who gives birth to a male child would be unclean for seven days.
What was a woman required to do following her being unclean?
She must wait about a month in the impurity of the blood she bled from giving birth. She must not enter the tabernacle or touch anything holy until that time is over.
What was a woman required to do differently if she gave birth to a female child?
If a woman gives birth to female child, she will be unclean for two weeks. The woman should wait about two months in the impurity of the blood she bled when she gave birth to the baby.
What was a woman required to do at the end of her purification?
At the end of her purification, a woman should bring a one-year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a pigeon or dove for a sin offering to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
What if the woman who gives birth to a child cannot afford a lamb?
If the woman cannot afford a lamb, she must bring two pigeons or two doves for the burnt and sin offerings.
What would happen to the woman after she did these things?
The woman will be clean after the priest makes atonement for her.
What did Yahweh should happen if someone has on his skin a swelling, scab, or bright spot that becomes infected?
Yahweh said that anyone who has a skin infection must be brought to Aaron or to one of his sons, the priests.
What must be done if the priest determines that the swelling, scab, or bright spot may not be infectious?
If the priest cannot determine that the swelling, scab, or bright spot is infectious, the priest must quarantine the person for one week.
What if the swelling, scab, or bright spot proves not to be infectious?
If the swelling, scab, or bright spot is not infectious, the priest will pronounce him clean and he must wash his clothes, and he will be clean.
What are the three conditions that the swelling, scab, or bright spot may show if it is to be declared infectious?
The three conditions which the swelling, scab, or bright spot may show to be pronounced infectious are white swelling in the skin, the hair has turned white, and there is raw flesh in the swelling.
If the priest determines that this is a chronic skin disease, what must the priest do?
If the priest determines that this is a chronic skin disease, he must pronounce the person unclean, but the priest does not isolate him.
If the skin disease covers the person’s entire body and living flesh can be seen, what is the person declared to be?
If the skin disease covers the person’s entire body and living flesh can be seen, the person is declared to be unclean.
How may the unclean person become clean again?
The unclean person may become clean again if the infection has been turned to white; the priest shall pronounce him clean.
What must a priest do if he examines a person who had a boil but now has a swelling or bright spot that appears deeper under the skin where the boil was, and the hair there has turned white?
The priest must pronounce that person unclean.
What kind of infectious disease may cause one to be unclean if it is found on the head or chin?
A scall, a skin disease of the head or the beard, may cause one to be unclean if it is found.
What would a man who lost his hair be pronounced?
A man whose head is made bare is clean. He is bald.
What one condition on a man’s bald head would result in the man being pronounced unclean?
If the bald man’s head has reddish-white sores that appear like a skin disease, the priest should pronounce him unclean.
What must the unclean person do to let others know that he is unclean?

The unclean person must tear his clothes, let his long hair hang down disheveled, cover his upper lip, and shout “Unclean, unclean” when in the presence of others. He must also live alone, outside the camp.
What must the owner do with any garment of wool or linen or leather or anything made of leather that was found to be infected with a rotting fungus?
If any garment of wool or leather or anything made from leather is found to be infected with a rotting fungus, the owner must burn it completely.
Where must the priest examine the diseased person on the day of his cleansing?
The priest must examine the diseased person at a place on the outside of the camp to see if the infection is healed.
What must the priest command the diseased person to bring for the pronouncement of his cleansing?
The priest should command the person to bring two live clean birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn, and hyssop.
After the priest sprinkled the mixture of blood, water, cedar wood and hyssop over the diseased person seven times, what did he do with the remaining bird?
After the priest sprinkled the mixture over the diseased person seven times, he released the living bird to fly into the fields.
What must the person being cleansed do after the priest has pronounced him clean?
The person being cleansed must wash his clothes, shave all of his hair, bathe himself in the water, and remain outside his tent for seven days.
On the eighth day, what animals should the person being cleansed bring to the priest?
On the eighth day, the person being cleansed must take to the priest two perfect male lambs and one perfect female lamb a year old.
If the person being cleansed is poor and cannot afford these sacrifices, what must he bring?
If the person being cleansed is poor and cannot afford the lambs, he must bring one lamb, one tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, and a log of oil.
Where does the priest place the oil that is used in the cleansing?
The priest places the oil on the lobe of the right ear and on the right thumb and on the right big toe. The remainder he should put on the head of the one being cleansed.
What must happen to the house if the infection is a malignant mold that spreads?
The owner must tear down the house and dispose of everything outside of the city if the infection is a malignant mold that spreads.
When must a priest pronounce a house to be unclean?
A priest house must pronounce a house unclean if a malignant infection has spread in the house.
How can the house be pronounced clean if the infection is stopped?
The priest will be able to purify the house with the blood of the bird, the fresh water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop branches, and the crimson thread.
What did Yahweh say to Moses and Aaron was the condition of a man who has a flow of from his flesh?
Yahweh said to Moses and Aaron that any man who has a discharge coming from his genitals is impure.
What happens to the person who touches the person who is unclean because he had a discharge?
Anyone who touches the unclean person will be unclean himself and must bathe in water and wash his clothes, and he is unclean until evening.
In what kind of water must the person being cleansed from an infected flow of fluid bathe?
The person being cleansed from an infected flow of fluid must bathe in fresh water.
What must the unclean man present to the priest for a sin offering and for a burnt offering?
The unclean man must present to the priest two doves or two pigeons, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.
What is the condition of anything or any person that has contact with a man’s semen?
They must be washed in water and will be unclean until evening.
How long will woman be impure as she menstruates?
She will be impure for seven days.
How long will a man be unclean if he sleeps with a woman who is menstruating, and her flow touches him?
He shall be unclean for seven days, and every bed on which he lies shall be unclean.
What is a woman to bring as a sacrifice on the eight day after her flow of blood stops?
She is to bring to the priest, to the entrance of the tent of meeting, two doves or two pigeons.
What did Yahweh tell Moses to warn Aaron not to do regarding entering into the Most Holy Place inside the curtain?
Yahweh told Moses to warn Aaron not to enter into the Most Holy Place, where Yahweh is present inside the curtain at just any time, so that Aaron will not die.
What must Aaron bring with him when he enters the Most Holy Place?
Aaron must bring with him a bull for a sin offering and a ram as a burnt offering.
What must Aaron do before he puts on the priestly garments?
Aaron must wash himself in water before putting on the priestly garments.
From whom must Aaron acquire two male goats and one ram?
Aaron should take two male goats and a ram from the flocks of the Israelite community.
Why must Aaron cast lots for the goats?
Aaron casts lots for the goats to choose which one to offer to Yahweh and which one to be the scapegoat.
What happens to the goat to which the lot falls to be the scapegoat?
The goat that the stones determine to be the scapegoat must be presented before Yahweh to make atonement by sending it away into the desert.
For whom does Aaron present the bull?
Aaron presents the bull as a sin offering for himself and his family.
What must cover the atonement lid of the Box of the Testimony so that Aaron will not die?
A cloud of incense must cover the atonement lid so that Aaron will not die.
Who else must be in the tent with Aaron when he makes atonement in the most holy place?
No one else must be in the tent when Aaron makes atonement in the most holy place.
What must Aaron do when he places his hands on the head of the living goat?
Aaron must confess over the living goat all the iniquity of the people of Israel, all their rebellion and all their sins.
What is Aaron to do with the priestly garments?
Aaron is to take off the priestly garments and leave them in the tent of meeting.
When did Yahweh say the day for making atonement should take place?
On the tenth day of the seventh month, he will make atonement for you to cleanse you from all your sins.
If a man kills an ox, lamb, or goat without bringing it to the entrance of the tent of the assembly to offer it as a sacrifice to Yahweh, of what sin is he guilty?

The man who kills an ox, lamb, or goat without bringing it to the entrance of the tent of the assembly to offer it as a sacrifice to Yahweh is guilty of shedding innocent blood and must be cut off from his people.
What was the purpose of this command?
The purpose of this command was to get the people to offer their sacrifices to Yahweh in front of the tent of meeting instead of in the open fields.
This statute would stop the people from offering sacrifices to the goat idols.
What does Yahweh say makes atonement?
Yahweh says that the blood makes atonement.
What does Yahweh say must be done to any animal or bird that is killed to eat by any of the people of Israel or any foreigner who lives among them?
Yahweh says that any of the people of Israel or a foreigner living among them who kills an animal or bird to eat must pour the blood from it and cover the blood with soil.
What must he do if he does not wash his clothes and bathe himself in water?
If he does not wash his clothes and bathe himself in water, then he is now responsible for addressing his wrongdoing.
What must a person do who has eaten an animal that has died or been torn apart by animals?
A person who has eaten an animal that has died or has been torn apart by animals must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will remain unclean until evening.
What two places did Yahweh tell the people they could not behave like the people there?
Yahweh told the people of Israel they could not behave like the Egyptians or Canaanites.
What is one group of people with whom God forbade Israelites to have sexual relations?
Yahweh told the people they could not have sexual relations with any close relative.
Why is a man not to have sexual relations with a woman during her menstruation?
A man may not have sexual relations with a woman during her menstruation, because during that time she is unclean.
What may the people not sacrifice to Molech?
The people may not sacrifice their children to Molech.
What two sexual relations do verses 22 and 23 forbid?
Verses 22 and 23 forbid sexual relations with other men or animals.
What happened to the people who lived in the land before the people of Israel?
The people, those who lived in the land before the people of Israel, defiled the land, and the land vomited them out.
What will happen to any of the people or the foreigners who live among them who do any of these detestable things?
God will remove from his people any of the people who do any of these abominable practices.
What two things did Yahweh tell the people they must do?
Yahweh told the people that they must respect their father and mother, and everyone should practice the Sabbath days and honor them.
Why did Yahweh tell the people to leave the corners of their fields unharvested and to leave some of the grapes on the vine or on the ground?
The unharvested grain and grapes must be left for the poor and the immigrants.
To whom should the people not show favoritism?
The people should not show favoritism to someone because he is poor or rich, but instead judge the neighbor righteously.
What are the people to do instead of taking vengeance or holding a grudge?
Instead of taking vengeance or holding a grudge, the people are to love their neighbor as themselves.
What must the people do when planting seeds in the field?
When planting in the field, the people must not plant two kinds of seed in the same field.
How long must a planter of a fruit tree wait before he can eat the fruit?
A planter of a fruit tree must wait until the fifth year before he can eat the fruit of the tree.
What were the people told not to do?
The people were told not to shave the corners of their heads and or trim the corners of their beads.
Whom did Yahweh tell the people to arise before and honor?
Yahweh told the people to rise before a person with gray hair and honor elderly people.
Why did Yahweh say that the people of Israel should love the immigrants as they love themselves?
Yahweh told the people to love the foreigner because the people of Israel were once foreigners in the land of Egypt.
What would happen to anyone among the people of Israel who gives their child to Molech?
Anyone who gives their child to Molech the people living in Israel should kill by throwing stones at him.
What would Yahweh do to the man if the people did not put him to death?
If the people do not put him to death, Yahweh says he will cut him off from his people.
To whom did Yahweh tell the people not to turn?
Yahweh told the people not to turn to the mediums and spiritists, those who talk to the dead.
What was the result of a man having sexual relations with another man?
A man who has sexual relations with another man has done something abominable and both must be executed.
If a woman has sexual relations with an animal, what must be done?
The woman and the animal must be executed.
How did Yahweh describe the land that he had given the people of Israel?
Yahweh called the land “a land flowing with milk and honey.”
For the death of which person must a priest make himself unclean?
A priest should make himself unclean for the death of a very close relative.
What restrictions were placed on the priests concerning their hair and beards?
Priests were not allowed to shave their heads or the edges of their beards.
What would happen to a priest’s daughter who defiled herself by becoming a prostitute?
A priest’s daughter who disgraces her father by becoming a prostitute must be burned.
What must a high priest avoid even if the dead person is his father or mother?
A high priest must not make himself unclean by entering a place where there is a dead body, even if his father or mother has died.
What kind of woman must the priest not marry?
The priest must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, or a woman who is a prostitute.
What kind of man did Yahweh not want to approach him to perform the offerings?
Yahweh did not want any man with a bodily defect to approach him.
Who does Yahweh he will cut off from before his face?
Yahweh says that no priest, while he is impure, should ever approach the sacred altar to present a sacrifice. If he does, that person shall be cut off from before Yahweh’s face.
What must a priest do when he touches anything that makes him unclean?
He must consider himself to be unclean until the evening, and he must not eat any of the special food set aside for the priests unless he first bathes himself.
What will happen to priests who do not follow Yahweh’s instructions?
Yahweh says that he will hold them responsible for their wrongdoing and kill them.
Who are the only people who may eat the sacred food?
The only persons who may eat anything that is holy are the priest and his family and slaves he bought or who were born in his household.
Can a priest’s daughter who has married someone who is not a priest eat the holy food?
She may not eat the holy food unless she is divorced or widowed without children and returns to live in her father’s house.
What must a man do who eats holy food by mistake?
If a man eats holy food by mistake, he must repay the priest to whom the food belonged and add one-fifth to the value of it.
What kind of animal would be accepted as a sacrifice?
It must be a male animal without blemish from the cattle, sheep, or goats.
What is the most important requirement for any animal that is to be sacrificed to Yahweh?
Any animal sacrificed to Yahweh must be unblemished.
How old must a calf, sheep, or goat be to be offered as a sacrifice to Yahweh?
A calf, sheep, or goat must be at least eight days old to be offered as a sacrifice to Yahweh.
When must a thank offering be eaten?
It must be eaten on the same day that it is sacrificed.
What does Yahweh say about work and the Sabbath?
Yahweh says that people may work for six days, but the seventh day, the Sabbath, is to be a day of rest.
What festival is to be celebrated on the fourteenth day of the first month?
The Passover to honor Yahweh is to be celebrated in the first month on the fourteenth day.
What festival follows Passover on the fifteenth day of the first month?
The Festival of Unleavened Bread follows Passover on the fifteenth day of this month.
What must the people bring to the priest after the first harvest in the land that Yahweh is going to give them?
The people must bring to the priest a sheaf of the first of your harvest in the land that Yahweh is going to give them.
What date did Yahweh set for the Day of Atonement?
Yahweh set the tenth day of the seventh month as the Day of Atonement.
What must the people not do on the Day of Atonement?
The people must not do any work on the Day of Atonement.
What festival did Yahweh say would take place on the fifteenth day of the seventh month?
Yahweh said that the Festival of Shelters for Yahweh would take place on the fifteenth day of the seventh month.
What must the people use to rejoice during the Festival of Shelters for Yahweh?
The people must use the best fruit from their trees, branches of palm trees, boughs of leafy trees, and willows from riverbanks to rejoice before Yahweh for seven days.
Where were the people of Israel to live during the Festival of Shelters?
The people of Israel were to live in small shelters for the seven days of the Festival of Shelters.
What must Aaron do with the pure oil the people are to bring him?
Aaron must keep a lamp burning outside of the curtain of the testimony in the tent of meeting from evening until morning continually.
What must the priest place in two rows of six each Sabbath?
Each Sabbath, the priest must place on the gold table twelve loaves of bread in two rows of six.
Who is allowed to eat the offering of the twelve loaves?
Aaron and his sons must eat it in the holy place.
What were the people of Israel told to do to the man who blasphemed Yahweh?
Yahweh told the people of Israel to take the man outside the camp, place their hands on him, and stone him to death.
What must happen to a man who kills another man?
He must certainly be put to death.
What did Yahweh say must be done to anyone who causes death or injury to another person?
Yahweh said to the people that what they have done to another should be done to them; an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth.
What did Yahweh say should be done after the fields and vineyards are planted, pruned, and harvested for six years?
Yahweh said that after six years of planting, pruning, and harvesting the fields and vineyards, in the seventh year there should be a Sabbath rest for the fields and vineyards.
What must be done on the forty-ninth year, the tenth day of the seventh month?
A loud trumpet must be blown everywhere during the forty-ninth year, on the tenth day of the seventh month.
What will the fiftieth year be called?
The fiftieth year will be called a year of jubilee.
What significant event must take place during a jubilee year?
During the jubilee year, property and slaves should be freed and returned to their families.
What should be eaten during the jubilee year?
Only the food that grows by itself should be eaten during the jubilee year.
What must the people consider when buying or selling land?

People should consider how many years there are to the next jubilee year. The more years there are, the more valuable is the land, because you are selling the number of crops you can harvest until the next jubilee.
How will Yahweh take care of his people during the seventh year, the Sabbath year, when crops are not to be grown?
Yahweh told the people that the harvest the sixth year will be enough crops to feed for them for three years, so there would be food for the seventh year.
What did Yahweh say to the people about permanent ownership of land?
Yahweh said the land must not be sold permanently to a new owner, because the land belonged to him.
What property is not to be returned during the jubilee year?
After a year, a house bought in a walled city will become permanent property of the man who bought it.
How are the people to treat a fellow countryman who becomes poor and can no longer provide for himself?
The people are to help him and not charge him interest or try to profit from him in any way.
How should the people treat a fellow countryman who has sold himself as a slave?
A fellow countryman who has sold himself as a slave the people should treat as a hired servant, not made to work like a slave.
What does Yahweh tell the people they should not make?
Yahweh says to the people they should not make idols.
What must the people do to make sure Yahweh sends rain and harvest?
Yahweh says the people must walk in his laws and keep his commandments in order to receive his rain and harvest.
What will Yahweh do to make the people safe?
Yahweh will remove the dangerous animals and cause there to be no raids or wars in the land.
If the people do what Yahweh tells them to do, what does he promise to do for them?
If the people do what Yahweh tells them to do, he promises to walk among them and be their God. They will continue to be his people.
What kind of disease and fever does Yahweh say he will send on Israel if they do not obey his commandments?
Yahweh says he will send disease and fever that would make them blind and slowly kill them if they did not obey his commandments.
What did Yahweh say he would do to the weather if Israel did not obey his commandments?
Yahweh said he would make the sky over them like iron (drought) and the land as hard as bronze.
What does Yahweh say he will do if the people refuse to obey his commandments and decrees?
Yahweh says if the people will not listen to him, he will punish them again and again for their sins.
Yahweh said if Israel would not listen to him, he would send dangerous animals against them. What did Yahweh say those animals would do?
Yahweh said those animals would kill their children, destroy their cattle and make them few in number.
If the people do not obey Yahweh, have they lost all hope?

No. Yahweh says that if the people will confess their sins, the sins of their fathers, and their unfaithfulness to Yahweh, and humbly admit they are guilty, he will keep the covenant he made with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham.
In spite of their sin, what does Yahweh promise to do?
Yahweh promises not to reject them or detest them so as to completely destroy them and do away with the covenant he made with them, because he is still Yahweh their God.
What is the purpose of the standard value?
The purpose of the standard value is to determine how much someone must pay to free another person from a vow to belong only to Yahweh.
What is the standard value of a man between the ages of twenty and sixty?
A man between the ages of twenty and sixty has a standard value of fifty shekels of silver.
What is the standard value of a woman between the ages of twenty and sixty?
A woman between the ages of twenty and sixty has the standard value of thirty shekels.
What if the one making the vow is unable to afford the standard value of the person he had dedicated?
If the one making the vow is not able to afford the standard value, he must take that person to the priest and the priest will set the price for freeing him to an amount that the person can pay.
What other things may the priest value that are to be presented to Yahweh?
The priest may also value an animal to be presented for sacrifice, a man’s house, or some of his land.
What must a man do with a field he has sanctified to Yahweh in the year of the jubilee?

When a man has sanctified a field to Yahweh and the year of the jubilee comes, the priest will figure the estimated value of the field up to the year of the jubilee and the man must pay its value on that day as a holy gift to Yahweh.
Which of the animals belongs only to Yahweh?
The firstborn of all the animals belongs only to Yahweh.
What part of the things dedicated to Yahweh may be sold or redeemed?
Nothing dedicated to Yahweh may be sold or redeemed.
If a man redeems any of his tithe, what must he add to it?
If a man redeems any of his tithe, he must add a fifth to its value.
Where was Moses when he spoke to Israel?
Moses was east of the Jordan in the wilderness, in the plain of the Jordan River valley.
When did Moses speak to the people of Israel, telling them all that Yahweh commanded him?
Moses spoke to the people in the fortieth year after they had left Egypt.
To whom had Yahweh promised to give the land?
Yahweh had promised to give the land to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and to their descendants.
Why did Moses feel he could not govern the people alone?
There were too many of them since God had multiplied them and made them as numerous as the stars of the heavens.
Who would help Moses solve all the problems and disputes of the people?
The people would choose wise, understanding, and well-known men from each tribe and appoint these men leaders to help Moses.
What did Moses command the judges to do?
He commanded them to hear and judge righteously concerning the quarrels and cases the Israelites had with each other or with any foreigner who lived among them.
Where did Israel travel through as they journeyed from Horeb to the hill country?
They traveled through all the great and terrible wilderness.
What did the people ask Moses to do before they would enter the land?
They asked Moses to send men ahead to explore the land and report back about it.
Who did Moses choose to scout out the land?
He chose one man from each of the 12 tribes.
What did the men report back about the land?
They reported that the land that Yahweh was giving them was good.
What were the people grumbling against Yahweh about?
They said Yahweh hated them and he brought them out of the land of Egypt to destroy them.
What did the spies say about the people of the land?
They said that the people of the land were stronger and taller than the Israelites and had fortified cities.
What did Moses say was the reason the people did not need to be afraid?
He told them not to be afraid, because Yahweh would go before them and would fight for them like he did in Egypt and in the wilderness.
What did Yahweh say when he became angry?
He said that not one of these men would see the good land except Caleb.
What did Yahweh tell Moses to do for Joshua, the son of Nun?
Yahweh told Moses to encourage Joshua for he would lead Israel to occupy the land.
Who did Yahweh say will go into the land and possess it?
He said their children will go in and will possess the land.
What did the people do when Yahweh told them not to attack the hill country?
They were arrogant and went up to the hill country to fight anyway.
Where did Moses say they journeyed?
They journeyed into the wilderness on the way to the Sea of Reeds.
What did Yahweh command the people to be careful not to do?
They were not to fight the descendants of Esau, who live near Mount Seir, for Yahweh had given that land to them.
How were they to get food and water?
They were to buy food and water from the people living there so they could eat and drink.
What did Yahweh tell them they were not to do in Moab?
They were not to trouble or fight with the people of Moab because Yahweh had given that land to them.
How long did it take Israel to go from Kadesh Barnea to the wadi of Zered?
It took them 38 years from when they left until they crossed wadi of Zered.
What happened to all the men who had been old enough to fight?
All the men who had been old enough to fight had died.
To whom had Yahweh given the land where the people of Ammon were living?
Yahweh had given that land to the descendants of Lot.
What will the people of the land do when they hear news about the Israelites?
They will tremble and be afraid because of what they hear about the Israelites.
What words of peace did Moses send to Sihon, king of Heshbon?
Moses asked that they be allowed to pass through his land, staying on the road and not turning to the right or left.
How did Moses plan to get food and water for the people?
He asked the king to sell him food and water so the Israelites could eat and drink.
What happened when Sihon came out to fight against Moses and his people?
Yahweh allowed Moses and his people to defeated him, killing him, his son, and all his people.
What happened to all the king’s cities?
Moses captured all the king’s cities and destroyed them, including women and children, leaving no survivors.
What did Og, the king of Bashan, do to Israel as they approached his land?
As Israel approached the land of Bashan, the king and all his soldiers came and attacked them.
What did Israel do to the king of Bashan and his people?
They defeated the king of Bashan, killing him and all his people, leaving no survivors.
What did Israel do with the cattle and the spoil of the cities?
They took for themselves all the cattle and the spoil of the cities.
To whom did Moses give the land that they had captured?
He gave it to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half of the tribe of Manasseh.
What did Moses command the men of war of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half of the tribe of Manasseh to do?
He commanded them to cross over the Jordan River to help the rest of the people of Israel conquer that land.
When did Yahweh say the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half of the tribe of Manasseh could return to their own land?
Yahweh said they could return to their own land after the rest of the Israelites captured the land that God was giving to them.
What did Moses tell Joshua not to do?
He told Joshua not to fear the enemy because Yahweh would be the one who would fight for him.
What did Moses ask Yahweh to allow him to do?
He asked Yahweh to let him go see the good land across the Jordan River and in Lebanon.
How did Yahweh respond to Moses’ request to go and see the land?
Yahweh was angry with Moses because of what the people had done and did not listen to his request.
What did Yahweh allow Moses to do?
Yahweh told him to go up to the top of Mount Pisgah and look all around from there, for he would not cross the Jordan River.
What did Yahweh tell Moses to do for Joshua?
He told Moses to instruct, encourage, and strengthen Joshua, because he would lead the people across the river to occupy the land that he could see.
What must the people of Israel do so that they may live and go in and possess the land that Yahweh is giving them?
They must listen and obey the laws that Moses will teach them so that they may possess the land.
What does Moses instruct the people not to do?
They must not add to or take away from the words of the commands Moses is giving them so they will obey the commandments of Yahweh.
What happened to the men who were worshiping Baal?
Yahweh destroyed the men that worshiped the Baal of Peor.
What will be the result of Israel keeping the rules that Moses commanded them?
The people around them will notice that because they keep these rules, they are a nation that has wisdom and understanding.
What should the people do so that they do not forget what God has done?
They should guard themselves by remembering the things God has done and telling them to their children and their grandchildren.
What did the people hear out of the middle of the fire on the mountain?
They heard Yahweh’s voice out of the middle of the fire but did not see him.
What was the covenant written on that Yahweh commanded them to obey?
The Ten Commandments that Yahweh gave to Moses for the people to obey were written on two tablets of stone.
What were the people told not to do so as to not act corruptly?
They were told not to make any carved figures or idols of any thing.
Why did Moses tell the people to be careful about the sun, moon, and stars?
He told them that they should be careful to not be seduced to worship the heavens, sun, moon, or stars.
Why did Yahweh bring the people out of Egypt?
He brought them out of Egypt to be a people who belong to him.
What did Yahweh declare to Moses because he was angry with him?
He declared that Moses would not cross the Jordan River into the good land.
Why did Yahweh forbid Israel to make any carved figure or idol?
Yahweh their God is a jealous God and wants them to worship only him.
What does Moses say will happen if the people corrupt themselves and do evil in Yahweh’s sight?
They will perish in the land over the Jordan and be completely destroyed.
What does Moses say Yahweh will do to the people if they worship idols?
Yahweh will scatter them among other nations and only a few would survive.
When will the people find Yahweh?
They will find him when they search for him with all their heart and all their soul.
What will make the people return to Yahweh their God and listen to his voice?
When they are in trouble and when all the bad things have come on them, they will return to Yahweh.
What did God do for the people when they were in Egypt?
God chose for himself all these people from the midst of another nation, by using his great power when he performed miracles, sent plagues, and fought the Egyptians for them.
What did Yahweh do to show the people that he alone is God?
He allowed them to hear his voice speak from heaven, and on earth he made them see his great fire and hear his voice coming from it.
What did Yahweh do for Israel because he loved their ancestors?
He chose their descendants and brought them out of Egypt with his great power. He gave them their land after driving out the more powerful nations.
Where could a person flee if he killed another person accidentally?
He could flee to one of the three cities that Moses had selected on the east side of the Jordan River.
What was included in the law that Moses gave the people of Israel?
He gave them the law which included all the instructions, rules, and regulations that he told them when they came out of Egypt.
From which two kings did Moses and his people take land on the east side of the Jordan River?
The Israelites took the land of Sihon, king of the Amorites, and Og, king of Bashan.
Where did Yahweh make his covenant with the people?
Yahweh made his covenant with the people of Israel at Horeb.
Why did Moses stand between Yahweh and the people when Yahweh revealed his word to them?
They were afraid of the fire from which Yahweh was speaking so Moses stood between them in order to tell them what he said.
Who does Yahweh tell Israel he is?
He told them that he is Yahweh their God, who brought them from the land of Egypt and freed them from slavery.
What does God tell Israel not make, bow down to, or serve?
They should not make carved figures of any likeness of anything that is in the sky, on earth, or in the water. If they do, God will punish them and their descendants.
What will Yahweh do for those who love him and keep his commandments?
He will show covenant faithfulness to those who love him and obey his commandments.
Who will Yahweh not leave unpunished?
He will not leave unpunished those who use his name for wrong purposes.
What does Yahweh say about the seventh day?
The seventh day is a day of rest which is dedicated to Yahweh their God, so they must not do any work.
What does Yahweh want them to remember when they observe the Sabbath day?
He wants them to remember that they were slaves in Egypt and that God brought them out by his great power.
What did Yahweh say would be the result if they honor their father and mother?
They will live a long time in the land that God gave them and things will go well for them there.
What were they commanded not to do?
They should not murder, commit adultery, steal, or give false witness.
On what did Yahweh write down his words?
He wrote his words down on two tablets of stone and gave them to Moses.
What did the people say would happen to them if they heard the voice of Yahweh any longer?
The people said that they would be burned up by the great fire and would die.
What did the people say they would do when Moses tells them everything that Yahweh says?
They said they will listen and obey Yahweh’s word.
What did Yahweh say about the response of the people?
Yahweh said he heard what the people said and that what they had spoken was good.
What did Moses say would happen to the people if they did all that Yahweh had commanded them?
If they keep the commandments, they will live a long time in the land and things will go well for them there.
What will happen if the Israelites and their children keep all Yahweh’s statutes and commandments all the days of your lives?
If they keep his statutes and commandments, they will live for a long time.
How did Moses describe the land into which the people were going?
He said that it was a land flowing with milk and honey.
They should love Yahweh with all their heart, all their soul, and all their strength.
When should the people diligently teach the commandments to their children?
They should teach the commandments to their children at every opportunity such as when they are in their house or walking on the road, lying down to rest, or getting up.
When should Israel remember what Yahweh has done for them?
They should remember that it was Yahweh who brought them into the land he had promised them when they are enjoying every good thing that Yahweh had given them that they did not have to work for.
What will happen to Israel if they worship the gods of the people around them?
Yahweh will become angry with them and he will destroy them completely if they worship the gods of the people around them.
What did the people do at Massah that they should not repeat?
They tested Yahweh by doing sinful things to see if he would punish them or not.
How should the people respond when their children ask about all the things that Yahweh commanded?
They should tell their children about how they were Pharaoh’s slaves and Yahweh brought them out of Egypt and gave them the land that he promised to their ancestors.
Why should the people fear Yahweh?
They should fear him so that things will go well for them and so that he will protect them as a nation.
What must the people do to the people of the land that Yahweh is bringing them into?
They must defeat them and destroy them completely.
What must the Israelites not do with the people of those nations?
They are not to make any covenants with them, show them mercy, or arrange any marriages with them for their sons or daughters.
How should Israel deal with anything associated with the idols of the people of these nations?
They should break down their altars, smash their sacred stone pillars, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their idols.
Did Yahweh keep his oath to their ancestors?
Yahweh kept his oath and rescued them from slavery to Pharaoh in Egypt.
What will Yahweh do with those who love him and keep his commandments?
Yahweh will keep his covenants with those who love him and keep his commandments and faithfully love them forever.
In what ways will the people be blessed by Yahweh if they keep his decrees?
God will love them and bless them and multiply them by giving them many children, crops, and animals.
What will God do to the nations of whom Israel is afraid?
God will make them experience the same kinds of great trials and other displays of his power that they saw in Egypt.
Why should the Israelites not be frightened of the people?
Yahweh, who is a great and fearsome God, will be with them.
How will God enable the people to defeat their enemies?
God will greatly confuse them in battle and cause them to panic until they are destroyed.
What are they to do to the idols of the gods of the nations?
They are to burn the idols and not even keep the gold or silver they are made of, as they are to be completely destroyed.
What should the people of Israel remember?
They should remember all the ways that Yahweh led them over those 40 years in the wilderness. He was testing them to find out if they would obey his commandments or not.
How and why did Yahweh humble them?
He allowed them to be hungry and then fed them manna so that they would know that they could not live only by having enough food to eat but also by paying attention to everything that Yahweh says.
How else did Yahweh provide for them all those years in the wilderness?
Their clothing did not wear out and their feet did not swell.
How did Yahweh instruct the Israelites?
As a man instructs and corrects his son, so Yahweh taught and corrected them.
What is in the good land into which God is bringing them?
The land will be filled with many sources of water, grain, fruit and olive trees, and honey.
What will cause the people to bless and thank Yahweh?
They will thank him because of the good and fertile land that he has given them.
What were the people reminded not to do?
They were reminded not to forget Yahweh by failing to obey his commandments.
Why might the people forget Yahweh who brought them out of Egypt?
When all that they possess increases, including herds, flock, and silver and gold, they might become proud and they might forget Yahweh.
How did Yahweh provide water and food in the terrible wilderness for the people of Israel?
Yahweh brought water out of solid rock for them to drink and provided manna for them to eat.
What would cause the people to perish like the nations around them?
They will perish if they forget their God and worship and serve other gods, because they would not listen to the voice of Yahweh.
Where are the people of Israel preparing to go?
Israel is about to cross over the Jordan.
What will happen when Israel crosses Jordan?
Yahweh will go ahead of them and will destroy the nations like a devouring fire.
What did Moses tell the people not to think after Yahweh enables them to drive their enemies out of the land?
He told them not to think that it was because of Israel’s righteousness that Yahweh gave them the land.
What is the reason God is driving the nations out?
He is driving them out because of their wickedness, and to keep his promise to Israel’s ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Why was Yahweh angry with the people of Israel?
He was angry with them because they were rebellious against him.
What did Moses eat and drink on the mountain?
He did not eat or drink anything for 40 days and 40 nights on the mountain.
Why did Yahweh tell Moses to quickly go down from the mountain?
Yahweh told him the people had corrupted themselves by doing what Yahweh had commanded them not to do and had made for themselves an idol to worship.
Why did Yahweh say he would destroy the Israelites?
Yahweh said he had seen that they were a stubborn people.
What did Moses find that Israel had made while he was on the mountain?
They had sinned against Yahweh by molding a calf as an idol just as he had commanded them not to do.
What did Moses do after he saw that the people had done evil in the sight of Yahweh?
He threw down the tablets and broke them before their eyes, he prostrated himself before Yahweh for 40 days and nights, and did not eat or drink because of their sin.
Why did Moses pray for the people and Aaron?
He prayed because Yahweh was angry enough with the people and with Aaron to destroy them.
What did Moses do to the calf that the people had made?
Moses burned it, crushed it, and ground it into dust and threw the dust into the stream that came down from the mountain.
How did the people provoke Yahweh to anger?
They rebelled against the commandment of Yahweh by not trusting him or obeying what he told them.
What was Moses praying as he prostrated himself before Yahweh for 40 days and nights?
He prayed that Yahweh would not destroy his people whom he had rescued and brought out of Egypt.
What was Moses thinking the people of Egypt would say if Yahweh destroyed his people?
He is afraid the people of Egypt would say that Yahweh was not able to bring Israel into the land he had promised them but that he took them into the wilderness to kill them because he hated them.
Where did Yahweh tell Moses to place the two tablets of stone on which he would write the words that were on the first tablets?
Yahweh told him he to place the two tablets of stone into the chest of wood that Moses would make.
What did Yahweh write on the tablets of stone when Moses went up the mountain with them?
Yahweh wrote the same Ten Commandments on the tablets that he had written on the first tablets.
Where did Moses put the two tablets when he returned from the mountain?
He put them into the chest that he had made as Yahweh commanded him.
Aaron died and was buried in Moserah and Eleazar, his son, took his place as priest.
What tribe had Yahweh chosen to carry the box of the covenant and to serve Yahweh?
Yahweh chose the tribe of Levi to carry the chest, to serve him, and to bless people in his name.
How long did Moses stay on the mountain this time?
He stayed on the mountain 40 days and 40 nights, just like he did the first time.
What does Moses say that Yahweh requires of Israel?
Yahweh requires Israel to fear him, walk in all his ways, love him, worship him with all their heart and soul, and to obey his commandments.
What did Moses tell the people to circumcise?
He told them to humble themselves as if they were circumcising the foreskin of their hearts.
Why should Israel love the foreigner?
Israel should love the foreigner because they were once foreigners in the land of Egypt.
How has God blessed the people since they first went down into Egypt?
There were only 70 of their ancestors who went down into Egypt but now, God has made them as numerous as the stars of the heavens.
What does Moses tell the people to always keep?
He tells them to always keep Yahweh’s rules, statutes, decrees, and commandments.
Who had not seen all that Yahweh did in Egypt?
The children of the Israelites who were born while they wandered in the wilderness had not seen Yahweh’s discipline and his mighty deeds that he did in Egypt.
How did Yahweh destroy the army of Egypt when they pursued after Israel?
Yahweh caused the water of the Sea of Reeds to drown the army of Egypt as they pursued after Israel.
The Israelites had seen all the great works that Yahweh did.
What will happen to the people if they keep all the commandments?
If they keep all the commandments, they will be strong, go in and possess the land, and they and their descendants will live in the land for a long time.
How is the land they are going to enter different from the land of Egypt?
In the land they are going to enter there are many hills and valleys and plenty of water from the rain.
What would Yahweh give them if they obey his commandments and to love and serve him with all their heart and soul?
Yahweh will give them rain in its season, that they may gather their grain and be able to make wine and oil.
What will Yahweh do if the people turn aside and worship other gods?
He will become angry and will restrain the heavens so there will not be any rain.
What should the people do so that they will live for a very long time in the land?
They will write the commandments on the doorposts of their house and on their gates.
If the people keep all the commandments of Yahweh and cling to him, what will he do for them?
Yahweh will drive out all the other nations that are larger and mightier than they are.
Why would no man be able to stand before Israel?
Yahweh will cause the people of that land to fear and feel terror of Israel.
What did Moses give Israel that day?
He gave them a blessing and a curse.
Where must the people go in order to possess the land?
They must cross over the Jordan to possess and live in the land.
What places did Moses tell Israel to destroy?
They were to destroy all the places where the nations that Israel dispossessed had worshiped their gods.
What does Yahweh instruct the people of Israel do to the name of the gods of the nations?
He told Israel to destroy everything to do with those gods in order to remove their name from there.
In what place were the people of Israel to bring their burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, and offerings?
They were to go to the place that Yahweh their God would choose.
What kinds of things were the people of Israel doing?
They were doing whatever they thought was right.
What kind of rest will Yahweh give to Israel when they go over the Jordan?
He will give them rest by protecting them from all their surrounding enemies, so they will live in safety.
What animals can Israel kill and eat?
Israel can kill and eat domesticated animals where they are living.
What was Israel not allowed to eat?
Israel was not allowed to eat the blood, but must pour it out on the earth.
Where was Israel told they could not eat their tithes and sacrifices?
They were not allowed to eat what was intended for tithing or sacrificing where they lived.
Where were the people of Israel to eat their tithes and sacrifices?
They were to eat these offerings in the place that Yahweh their God will choose.
What was Israel told be sure not to do?
They were told to not forget to take care of the Levites.
What can Israel eat when Yahweh their God enlarges their borders as he has promised them?
Israel can eat the meat from the new land.
What can Israel eat if the place that Yahweh their God chooses to put his name is too far from them?
If the place that Yahweh Israel’s God chooses to put his name is too far from where they live, then they may kill some of their flock for sacrifices as well as to eat.
Where did they consider the life of the animal?
Israel was to consider the blood as the life of the animal and thus should not eat it with the meat.
What is Israel instructed to take to the place that Yahweh chooses?
Israel is to take the sacred things that they have and their offerings to the place that Yahweh chooses.
What is to be done with the blood and the meat of the animals they offer as a burnt offering?
They are to pour the blood out on the altar of Yahweh their God and eat the meat.
What is Israel instructed to do so that it may go well with them and with their descendants after them?
Israel is to listen to and obey all the words that Yahweh commands them and do what is good and right so that things may go well for them and their descendants forever.
What does Yahweh instruct Israel to watch out for when God enables Israel to go in and dispossess the nations in the land and live there?
Israel is to pay attention so that they are not trapped into serving the gods of those nations.
What have the other nations done to their sons and daughters in order to worship the gods?
The other nations have even burned their sons and daughters on altars to these other gods.
Why should the people of Israel not listen to a prophet who predicts something that happens and then says that they should go after other gods and worship them?
The people of Israel should not listen because Yahweh is testing them to know whether they love him with all their heart and with all their soul.
What should the people of Israel do to the prophet who tells them to worship other gods?
They should put that prophet to death because he has spoken against what Yahweh has commanded them.
What have the people of Israel been instructed to do to anyone who secretly entices them and says that they should go and worship other gods?
They must surely kill anyone who entices them to worship other gods.
How should the people of Israel kill the person who tells them to disobey Yahweh their God?
They should stone that person to death.
What shall the people of Israel do if they hear that some wicked person is telling others to go and worship other gods?
They should investigate it thoroughly to see if it is true.
What should Israel do to a city if they learn that it is true that the inhabitants have been worshiping other gods?
They should kill the inhabitants of that city and destroy everything in it.
What are the people told about the things that Yahweh has told them to destroy?
They must not take any of those things for themselves that Yahweh has told them to destroy, so that Yahweh will not be angry and will have compassion on them as he promised their ancestors.
What does Moses instruct the people of Yahweh not to do?
They are not to cut themselves nor shave any part of their heads for the dead.
What are the two characteristics of the animals that the Israelites are allowed to eat?
Israel may eat any animal that has split hooves and also chews the cud.
Why is the pig not to be eaten?
The pig is unclean for the Israelites because he has split hooves but does not chew the cud.
What are the characteristics of the things from the water that the Israelites are allowed to eat?
They may eat whatever has fins and scales.
Are the Israelites allowed to eat winged swarming things?
All winged, swarming insects are unclean for the Israelites and must not be eaten.
May the Israelites eat anything that dies of natural causes?
They may not eat anything that dies naturally, but they may give it to a foreigner to eat or sell.
What could the Israelites not do with a young goat?
They must not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.
What are the Israelites to do with the crops produced in their fields?
Israelites must set apart a tenth of all their crops once a year.
What are the Israelites instructed to eat in the place that he will choose?
Israel must eat the tithe, which was a tenth of their grain, new wine, and of their oil, as well as the firstborn animals in the place that Yahweh will choose.
What are the Israelites allowed to do if they are blessed with such a large crop that they are not able to carry the tithe to the place that Yahweh will choose?
If the journey is too for them to carry all of the tithe of what Yahweh has blessed them with, they can sell a tenth of their crops and take the money to the place that Yahweh has chosen.
Who has no inheritance with the Israelites and must not be neglected?
The Levites will not own any land so the others must not neglect to help them.
What are the Israelites instructed to do at the end of every three years?
At the end of every three years the Israelites are to store the tithe of their produce from that year for the Levites, the foreigners, the fatherless, and the widows to have enough to eat.
What must the Israelites do at the end of every seven years?
At the end of every seven years the Israelites must cancel all debts.
Why are debts to be canceled every seven years?
Everyone will cancel that which he has loaned to a fellow Israelite because Yahweh has declared the cancelation of debts every seven years.
From whom can Israelites continue to collect payment at the end of every seven years?
The Israelites can continue to collect payment of a debt from a foreigner.
Why should there be no poor among the Israelites?
If they do all that Yahweh has commanded them, there should no longer be poor among them since Yahweh will bless them.
What will happen to demonstrate that Yahweh has blessed Israel as he promised?
Israel will lend to many nations, but will not borrow; Israel will rule over many nations, but the other nations will not rule over them.
What are the Israelites told not to do if there is a poor man among them?
The Israelites are told not to be selfish and refuse to help them.
What should the Israelites be careful not to do when the seventh year, the year of remission is near?
They should not refuse to give help to a poor man because the year of canceling debts is near.
What will Yahweh do for the Israelites in return for giving generously to the poor?
Yahweh will bless the Israelites in everything they do.
Why is Israel commanded to give generously to their fellow Israelites, to the needy and the poor in their land?
They should give generously because there will always be poor living among them.
What are Israelites instructed to give a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman who is released to go free in the seventh year?
They must provide for that person freely out of their flocks and their crops with which Yahweh their God has blessed them.
What are the Israelites to remember as they give to the one they set free?
The Israelites are told to remember that they were slaves in the land of Egypt and Yahweh freed them.
What is an Israelite to do to a male or female slave who says that they do not want to leave?
The Israelite is to pierce the slave’s ear, and he or she will be their slave forever.
Why should it not seem difficult for the Israelite to let the slave go free?
It should not be difficult because he has served them for six years and given them twice the value of a hired person.
What must the people of Israel do with the firstborn males in their herd and their flock?
They must set them aside for Yahweh and not use them for work or shear them.
What are the Israelites to do with the firstborn animal if it is lame or blind or has any other defect?
They must not sacrifice it to Yahweh, but instead they can eat it.
Why are the Israelites to keep the Passover for Yahweh their God in the month of Aviv?
The Israelites are to celebrate the Passover each year during the month of Aviv because Yahweh brought Israel out of Egypt in that month.
What will the Israelites do to celebrate the Passover?
The Israelites will sacrifice some of the flock and the herd in the place that Yahweh will choose.
Why are the Israelites to eat no leavened bread or have yeast in all their land for seven days?
They are to eat no leavened bread or have yeast during those days to remind them that they came out of the land of Egypt with too much haste for bread to rise.
What are the Israelites told about the meat that they sacrifice in the evening on the first day?
The Israelites are to make sure there is no meat that they sacrifice in the evening remaining the next morning.
Where are the Israelites to offer the sacrifice of the Passover?
They are to sacrifice at the place that Yahweh will choose.
When will the sacrifice of the Passover be performed?
The sacrifice of the Passover is to be performed in the evening when the sun is setting, at the time when the Israelites started to leave Egypt.
What are the Israelites supposed to do on the first six days as they celebrate Passover?
The Israelites are to eat unleavened bread for six days.
What are the Israelites supposed to do on the seventh day as they celebrate Passover?
On the seventh day, they are to have a festive assembly and do no work.
How do the Israelites determine the start of the Festival of Weeks for Yahweh?
The Israelites will count seven weeks from the time they begin to harvest their grain.
What contribution do the Israelites give on the Festival of Weeks?
They must give Yahweh a freewill offering according to how much Yahweh has blessed them.
What must they remember during the Festival of Weeks?
They must remember that they were slaves in Egypt.
What festival are the Israelites instructed to keep for seven days after they have gathered in the harvest from their threshing floors and from their wine presses?
They are to keep the Festival of Shelters for seven days after they have gathered in their harvest.
How much is every male Israelite supposed to give to Yahweh instead of coming without an offering?
Every male Israelite is to give in proportion to how much Yahweh has blessed him with that year.
At what the three festivals must all the males of Israel gather to worship Yahweh at the place that Yahweh chooses?
They must gather to worship Yahweh at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and at the Festival of Shelters.
Where are the Israelites to find their judges and officers?
The judges and officers will be taken from each of their tribes to judge the people with righteous judgment.
Why are the judges not to show partiality or take a bribe?
If a judge takes a bribe, he will find it difficult to judge fairly but will instead want to do what the person who bribes him wants him to do.
Why must the judges pursue righteousness and judge fairly?
They must pursue righteousness and judge fairly, so that they may live and occupy the land that Yahweh is giving them.
What are the Israelites not to set up for themselves?
They are not to set up an Asherah pole or a stone pillar to worship any idol.
Why must the Israelites not sacrifice an ox or a sheep with any blemish or defect to Yahweh?
A sacrifice that is not perfect will be detestable to Yahweh.
What are the Israelites told to do if they hear that a man or woman within their cities have done what is evil in the sight of Yahweh and is serving other gods?
The Israelites are to investigate thoroughly to know if this is true and that the idol worship is actually happening.
What are the Israelites to do with a man or woman who has done such an evil thing as worshiping other gods?
The Israelites are to stone that person to death.
How many witnesses are needed to convict a person to death?
Two or three witnesses are needed to convict a person to death.
Who must throw the first stones when putting a person to death?
The witnesses must be the first to throw the stones, followed by the rest of the people of Israel.
Why must the Israelites stone the person to death who has done this evil action of worshiping other gods?
This will get remove this evil from among them.
Who is to judge if the Israelites have a matter that is too hard for them to judge?
They must go to the place that Yahweh will choose, and explain the case to the Levites who are serving as priests and to the judge who is serving at that time and they will make the decision.
What man must die in order to remove the evil from Israel?
Anyone who acts arrogantly and does not listen to the decision of the priest or judge, must die to remove the evil from Israel.
How will the Israelites decide who to set up as a king over them at the time when they are in the land?
Israelites will select from among their fellow Israelites someone whom Yahweh will choose.
Why must the king of Israel not own multiple horses, nor send anyone back to Egypt to buy more horses?
He must not send anyone back to Egypt to buy more horses for him because Yahweh has told the Israelites to never return to Egypt.
Why is the king told not to have many wives?
He is not to marry a lot of wives because they might cause his heart to turn away from Yahweh.
What is the king instructed to do so that he may learn to honor Yahweh his God, and keep and obey all of his law?
He must write for himself a copy of this law on a scroll from which he is to read every day of his life.
Why is the king instructed to keep the scroll of the law with him?
He must read from the scroll daily so that he does not think he is more important than his fellow Israelites, and so that he will completely obey the commandments.
Why would the Levites be allowed to eat from the offerings given to Yahweh?
The Levites would be able to eat the offerings because they would not receive land as an inheritance like the other Israelites.
What was to be given to the priests from the sacrifices of the people?
From the sacrifices of the people, the priests were to be given the shoulder, two cheeks, and stomach of the oxen and sheep and the first parts of their grain, wine, oil, and fleece of the sheep.
Why were the priests supposed to receive these portions from the sacrifices of the people?
They were to receive these portions because Yahweh chose them from among the tribes to serve as priests in his name.
Which Levites can serve in the place that Yahweh will choose?
Any Levite who wants to can serve as a priest in the place that Yahweh will choose.
What were some of the disgusting practices followed by the other nations in the land?
Some of the disgusting practices were sacrificing their children, using divination, practicing magic, using sorcery, and talking with the dead or spirits.
Why will Yahweh drive out the nations from the land?
Yahweh will drive out the nations from the land because he hates the disgusting things they do and he wants his people to stay away from those things.
Who did Yahweh promise to raise up from among the people?
Yahweh promised he would raise up a prophet like Moses for them to obey.
When must a prophet be executed?
A prophet must be executed if he speaks a prophecy in Yahweh’s name that Yahweh has not commanded him to speak, or he speaks in the name of other gods.
What does it mean if a prophecy spoken in Yahweh’s name does not happen?
If a prophecy does not happen, then the prophecy is something that Yahweh has not spoken.
Why did Yahweh instruct the people to select three cities?
He instructed the people to select three cities so that everyone who kills another person could flee to one of them for safety.
Why should the one who kills another flee to a safe city?
He should flee so that the relative of the victim does not pursue him in anger and kill him.
What provision does Yahweh make for the person who kills another person by accident?
Yahweh provided three cities to which that person could flee and live.
What would be the conditions for adding three more cities for people to escape to?
If Yahweh enlarged their borders, then they must add three more cities for people to escape to.
What should happen if a person ambushes and kills someone and then flees to one of these cities?
The elders of this man’s city must bring him back and turn him over to the victim’s relative so that the attacker may be executed.
How many witnesses are needed for someone to be punished for their sin?
There must be two or three witnesses for anyone to be punished for their sin.
What should be done when controversy exists between two men?

Then the two men who have a controversy must go before the priests and the judges who are serving at that time. The judges will inquire thoroughly to see if the witness falsely testified against the other.
What must be done if a witness is found to be false?
If the testimony of a witness is found to be false, then they must do to him as he had planned to do to the person he accused.
Why must the people of Israel not be afraid when they go out to battle against their enemies?
The people of Israel must not be afraid because Yahweh their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, will be with them.
What should the priests do when the people of Israel draw near to the battle?
The priest should speak to the people and tell them not to be afraid because Yahweh is with them to fight for them.
What should a man do if he has built a new house and not yet dedicated it?
He should return to his house so he does not die in battle and another man dedicate it.
What should a man do if he is engaged to a woman and not yet married her?
He should return and marry her so he does not die in battle and another man marry her.
What was to happen if the people in a city far from Israel accepted the Israelites’ offer of peace?
All the people found in that city were to become forced labor for the Israelites and serve them.
What must happen if the city does not accept the offer of peace, but instead makes war against Israel?
Israel must attack it and when Yahweh gives Israel victory they must kill every man in it.
Why must the people of Israel utterly destroy everything that breathes in the cities of the land which Yahweh will give them as an inheritance?
They must destroy everything so that the people of the land do not teach them to do disgusting things for their gods, which would cause them to sin against Yahweh.
What should Israel do with the trees in the cities which they have under siege?
Israel should not cut down the trees that are used for food, but they can cut down the trees that are not used for food to build structures for attacking the city.
What should happen if someone who has been killed is found lying in a field and it is not known who killed him?
The elders and judges should measure to determine the nearest city to where the body was found.
