The word was good in the eyes of the sons of Israel; they blessed God and did not speak of going up against them to war to destroy their land.
What did Joshua do when he had aged and come into days, having Yahweh given Israel rest?
Joshua called to all of Israel, to its elders, heads, judges, and officers, and spoke to them.
Who did Joshua remind the people had fought for them against all the nations?
Joshua reminded them that Yahweh their God was the one who had fought for them.
What did Joshua warn the people not to do regarding the nations remaining among them and their gods?
Joshua warned them not to come among these nations, nor invoke the name of their gods nor swear by them nor serve them nor bow down to them.
What did Joshua, knowing he was about to die, affirm about all the good words Yahweh had spoken concerning Israel?
He affirmed that Yahweh he has done every single thing he promised to do for you.
What did Joshua warn would happen if the people transgressed Yahweh’s covenant by serving and bowing to other gods?
Joshua warned that if they did so, Yahweh’s anger would burn against them, and very soon none of them would be living in the good land that he gave them.
Where did Joshua gather all the tribes of Israel, and who presented themselves before God?
Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, and he called to the elders of Israel, its heads, judges, and officers, and they presented themselves before God.
What did Yahweh say, through Joshua, he had given to the people of Israel that they did not labor for, build, or plant?
Yahweh said he had given them land for which they had not labored, cities they had not built (but dwelled in), and vineyards and olive groves they did not plant (but ate from).
Whom did Joshua declare that he and his house would serve, regardless of the people’s choice?
Joshua declared that he and his house would serve Yahweh.
How did the people respond to Joshua’s challenge, affirming their commitment to serve Yahweh?
The people said, “We ourselves will serve Yahweh, for he is our God.”
What did Joshua warn would happen if Israel forsook Yahweh and served foreign gods, even after Yahweh had done good to them?
Joshua warned that if they forsook Yahweh and served foreign gods, then Yahweh would turn and do harm to them and destroy them, even after he has done such good things for them.
What was the people’s final declaration to Joshua regarding serving Yahweh and listening to his voice?
The people said to Joshua, “We will serve Yahweh our God, and we will listen to his voice.”
What did Joshua do to formalize the covenant, and where did he set up a great stone?
Joshua wrote these words in the book of the instruction of God, took a great stone, and set it up there beneath the oak tree that was at the Holy Place of Yahweh.
What did Joshua say the great stone would be a witness against them for, lest they deal falsely with their God?

Joshua told all the people, “Look! This stone will always be for a witness against us. This is the place where I told you what Yahweh wanted to say to you {and you promised that you would serve him}. This stone will remind you of your promise so that you are not disloyal to God.”
How old was Joshua, the servant of Yahweh, when he died?
Joshua, the son of Nun, the servant of Yahweh, died at the age of 110 years.
Whose bones, brought up from Egypt by the sons of Israel, did they bury in Shechem?
The sons of Israel buried the bones of Joseph, which they had brought up from Egypt, in Shechem.
Who would lead the people of Israel when they went up against the Canaanites to fight against them?
Judah would lead the people of Israel against the Canaanites to fight against them.
Against whom did the soldiers of Judah fight?
The soldiers of Judah fought against the Canaanites, the Perizzites, and Adoni-Bezek.
Who gathered their food from under Adoni-Bezek’s table?
Seventy kings, who had their thumbs and their big toes cut off, gathered their food from beneath Adoni-Bezek’s table.
What was the previous name of Hebron?
The name of Hebron was previously Kiriath Arba.
What did Caleb give to Othniel?
Caleb gave Achsah, his daughter, to be Othniel’s wife.
Since Achsah was given land in the Negev, what did she want her father to give her?
Since Achsah now had land in the Negev, she wanted him to give her springs of water.
Where is the wilderness of Judah?
The wilderness of Judah is in the Negev.
Why could the people of Judah not drive out the dwellers of the valley?
They could not drive out the dwellers of the valley because they had iron chariots.
Why did the Jebusites live with the people of Benjamin in Jerusalem?
Because the people of Benjamin did not drive out the Jebusites who inhabited Jerusalem, the Jebusites lived with the people of Benjamin in Jerusalem.
What happened to the man who showed the spies from the house of Joseph how to get into Bethel?
The spies let the man and his family get away.
When Israel became strong, what did they do to the Canaanites?
When Israel became strong, they forced the Canaanites to serve them with hard labor, but they never drove them out completely.
Why did the tribe of Asher live among the Canaanites?
The tribe of Asher lived among the Canaanites because they did not drive the Canaanites out of the land.
Who conquered the Amorites at Mount Heres, in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim?
The house of Joseph conquered them.
Where did the angel of Yahweh bring the people of Israel?
The angel of Yahweh brought them to the land he swore to give to their fathers.
When the angel said he would not drive the Canaanites out before the people of Israel, what did they do?
When the angel said he would not drive the Canaanites out before the people of Israel, they cried out and wept.
How long did the people serve Yahweh?
The people served Yahweh during the lifetimes of Joshua and of the elders who outlived him.
What gods did the people of Israel go after?
The people of Israel went after the gods of the peoples who were around them.
What had Yahweh sworn to Israel?
Yahweh had sworn that wherever Israel went out to fight, Yahweh would allow their enemies to defeat them.
The judges saved the people of Israel from the power of those who were stealing their possessions.
What happened when the judge died?
When the judge died, the people of Israel would turn away and do things that were even more corrupt than their fathers had done.
Why would Yahweh not drive out from Israel any of the nations that Joshua left when he died?

Yahweh would not drive out from Israel any of the nations that Joshua left when he died, so that Yahweh could test Israel to see whether or not they would do what Yahweh wanted them to do as their ancestors had.
Why did Yahweh leave nations to test Israel?
Yahweh left nations to test Israel to teach warfare to the new generation of the Israelites who had not known it before.
What would Yahweh do by means of the remaining nations?
Yahweh would test Israel by means of the remaining nations to confirm whether they would obey the commandments he gave their ancestors through Moses.
What did the people of Israel serve?
They served the Baals and the Asherahs.
Who did Yahweh first raise up, who would come to help the people of Israel?
Yahweh first raised up Othniel, the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.
Who gave strength to Eglon, the king of Moab?
Yahweh gave strength to Eglon, the king of Moab.
When did Yahweh raise up Ehud to help the people of Israel?
Yahweh raised up Ehud to help the people of Israel when they cried out to him for help.
Where did Ehud strap on the sword he made?
He strapped it on under his clothing on his right thigh.
Who was with Ehud and the king when Ehud told him the message?
Only Ehud and the king were there.
Why did fat close over the handle of the sword?
Fat closed over the handle because Ehud did not draw the sword out of the king’s body.
When the king’s servants saw that the doors of the upper room were bolted, what did they think?
When the king’s servants saw that the doors of the upper room were bolted, they thought he was relieving himself in the coolness of the upper room.
While the servants were waiting, wondering what they should do, Ehud escaped.
How did the people of Israel prevent the Moabites from crossing the river?
The people of Israel captured the fords of the Jordan across from the Moabites.
With what did Shamgar kill 600 Philistines?
Shamgar killed the Philistines with a stick used to goad the cattle.
Why did the people of Israel call out to Yahweh for help?
The people of Israel called out to Yahweh for help because Sisera had 900 iron chariots and he had been oppressing the people of Israel for 20 years.
Why did the people of Israel come to Deborah?
The people of Israel came to Deborah to settle their disputes.
Where would Yahweh make Sisera meet Barak?
Yahweh would make Sisera meet Barak by the river of Kishon.
Why would Yahweh make a woman defeat Sisera?
Yahweh would make a woman defeat Sisera because Barak would not go without Deborah.
From whom did the Kenites descend?
The Kenites descended from Hobab, Moses’ father-in-law.
How many of the army of Sisera survived?
None of the army of Sisera survived.
Why did Sisera go to the tent of Jael?
Sisera went to the tent of Jael because there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor, and the house of Heber, Jael’s husband.
When Sisera asked for water, what did Jael give him?
When Sisera asked for water, Jael gave him milk.
Jael hammered the tent peg into the side of his head and it pierced through him and went down into the ground.
The earth shook when Yahweh went out from Seir, when he marched from Edom.
What was not seen among 40,000 in Israel?
Neither shields nor spears were seen among 40,000 in Israel.
What things were used as saddles on the white donkeys?
Carpets were used as saddles on the white donkeys.
Why did the people of Yahweh come down?
The people of Yahweh came down to help Barak fight against the warriors.
The people of Zebulun would risk their lives to the point of death.
What fought against Sisera from their courses across the heavens?
The stars fought against Sisera as they moved across the heavens.
Why did the angel of Yahweh curse Meroz?
The angel of Yahweh cursed Meroz because they did not come to help Yahweh.
To what did Jael put her hand?
In one hand she took the tent peg and in her other hand, a workman’s hammer.
Where did the mother of Sisera look out?
The mother of Sisera looked out of a window through the lattice.
Like what should those who love Yahweh be?
Those who love Yahweh should be as strong as the sun when it rises.
What did the people of Israel do because of Midian?
To hide from the cruelty of Midian, the people of Israel made dens and caves in the mountains to live in.
What happened any time the Israelites planted their crops?
Any time the Israelites planted their crops, the Midianites, the Amalekites, and the people from the east would attack the Israelites.
How many Midianites and Amalekites would attack?
So many Midianites and Amalekites would attack that it was impossible to count them.
In whose land were the people of Israel living?
They were living in the land of the Amorites.
Why was Gideon separating out the wheat by beating it on the floor in the winepress?
Gideon was working in the winepress in order to hide from the Midianites.
What did Gideon think Yahweh had done to the people of Israel?
Gideon thought Yahweh had forsaken them and had allowed the people of Midian to rule over them.
Why did Gideon think he could not deliver Israel?
Gideon thought he could not deliver Israel because his family was the weakest in Manasseh and he was the youngest in his family.
Why did Yahweh wait for Gideon?
Yahweh waited for Gideon to bring him an offering.
Where did the angel of God tell Gideon to put the meat and unleavened bread?
The angel of God told Gideon to put the meat and unleavened bread on a rock.
What happened when the angel of Yahweh stretched out the end of the staff in his hand?
When the angel of Yahweh stretched out the end of the staff in his hand, touching the meat and the unleavened bread, a fire went up out of the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened bread.
Why was Gideon afraid when he understood that he had seen the angel of Yahweh?
Gideon was afraid when he understood that he had seen the angel of Yahweh because he thought he would die.
What did Yahweh tell Gideon to build on the top of the stronghold?
Yahweh told him to build an altar to Yahweh on the top of the stronghold.
Why did Gideon do what Yahweh told him to do at night?
Gideon did what Yahweh told him to do at night because he was too afraid of his father’s household and the men of the city to do it during the day.
Why did the men of the town want to put Gideon to death?
The men wanted to put Gideon to death because he tore down the altar of Baal and because he cut down the Asherah beside it.
Why was Gideon given the name, “Jerubbaal”?
Gideon was given the name “Jerubbaal” because it meant “Let Baal defend himself” and they said that Baal should be the one to punish him, since it was his altar Gideon had torn down.
What did Gideon do to find out if Yahweh intended to use him to save Israel?
Gideon put a woolen fleece on the threshing floor. He said that if there was dew only on the fleece, and if it was dry on all the ground, then he would know that Yahweh would use him to save Israel.
When Gideon squeezed the fleece and wrung out the dew, how much water was there?
When Gideon squeezed the fleece and wrung out the dew, there was enough water to fill a bowl.
What was Gideon’s second test for God?
Gideon’s second test was for God to make the fleece dry, and let there be dew on all the ground around it.
Why did Yahweh have the fearful soldiers return?
Yahweh had the fearful soldiers return so that Israel could not boast against Yahweh saying that their own power had saved them.
Why did Yahweh tell Gideon to take the soldiers down to the water?
Yahweh said that there were still too many soldiers and this would be the way that he would tell Gideon which ones would go with him.
How did Yahweh tell Gideon to separate the soldiers?
Yahweh told Gideon to set apart everyone who lapped up the water as a dog laps from those who knelt down to drink.
How many soldiers did Gideon keep?
Gideon kept 300 soldiers and sent the rest home.
If Gideon was afraid, what would strengthen Gideon’s courage?
If Gideon was afraid, he was told to go down to the camp and listen to what they were saying, and his courage would be strengthened to attack the camp.
When one man was telling a dream to his companion, who did the companion say the dream was about?
When one man was telling a dream to his companion, the companion said the dream was about Gideon. God had given him victory over Midian and all their army.
What did Gideon give his 300 soldiers?
Gideon gave them all ram’s horns and empty jars, with a torch inside each jar.
When did Gideon’s men blow the trumpets and break the jars that were in their hands?
Just as the Midianites were changing the guard, Gideon’s men blew on the ram’s horns and broke the jars that were in their hands.
When the soldiers blew the three hundred shofars, what did Yahweh do?
When they blew the three hundred shofars, Yahweh set every Midianite man’s sword against his comrades and against all their own army.
How far did the men of Ephraim take control of the waters?
The men of Ephraim put guards at the shallow river crossings as far as Beth Barah and the Jordan River.
Why did the men of Ephraim argue with Gideon?
The men of Ephraim argued with Gideon because he had not called them to help him when he went to fight against Midian.
For what did Gideon ask the men of Succoth?
Gideon asked the men of Succoth for loaves of bread for his soldiers.
Why did Gideon tell the men of Penuel that he would pull down the tower?
Gideon told the men of Penuel that he would pull down the tower because they would not give his army bread, just as the men of Succoth had refused.
Why did Gideon defeat the enemy army past Nobah and Jogbehah?
Gideon defeated the enemy army because they were feeling safe and not expecting an attack.
Whom did Gideon show to the men of Succoth before he punished them?
Gideon showed Zebah and Zalmunna to the men of Succoth before he punished them.
What men did Zebah and Zalmunna kill at Tabor?
Zebah and Zalmunna killed Gideon’s brothers.
Why did Jether not draw his sword?
Jether did not draw his sword for he was afraid; he was still a young boy.
Who did Gideon say would rule over the men of Israel?
Gideon said Yahweh would rule over the men of Israel.
For what did Gideon ask the men of Israel?
Gideon asked them for the earrings from their spoil.
What did Gideon make out of the earrings?
Gideon made an sacred garment out of the earrings.
What did Israel do to the golden ephod?
What happened as soon as Gideon was dead?
As soon as Gideon was dead, the people of Israel turned again and worshiped the Baals.
Abimelech’s father was Gideon who was also called Jerubbaal.
Why did the leaders of Shechem agree to follow Abimelech?
They agreed to follow Abimelech because he was their relative.
For what did Abimelech use the 70 pieces of silver?
Abimelech used the 70 pieces of silver to hire wicked and violent men.
Jotham was not murdered because he hid himself.
On what day did Jotham address the leaders of Shechem?
Jotham addressed them on the same day that they had risen up against his father’s house and killed 70 of his sons.
What was the curse of Jotham?
The curse of Jotham was for fire to come out from Abimelech to burn up the men of Shechem and Beth Millo, and for fire to come out from the men of Shechem and Beth Millo to burn up Abimelech.
Why did God allow the leaders of Shechem to deal treacherously with Abimelech?
God allowed the leaders of Shechem to deal treacherously with Abimelech so that the violence done to the 70 sons of Jerubbaal might be avenged.
Who did the leaders of Shechem hope to ambush?
The leaders of Shechem hoped to ambush Abimelech.
Who wished the people would serve him instead of Abimelech?
Gaal wished the people would serve him.
When Zebul heard what Gaal was saying about removing Abimelech, he became angry.
Why did Zebul send messengers to Abimelech?
He sent messengers to Abimelech in order to warn him that Gaal, the son of Ebed, was inciting the city against him.
How did Zebul describe the men Gaal saw coming down the hills?
Zebul said they were shadows of the hills.
What did Zebul tell Gaal to do?
Zebul told Gaal to go out and fight against Abimelech.
What happened when Gaal fought Abimelech?
Abimelech pursued Gaal, and Gaal fled before Abimelech, and many fell with deadly wounds before the entrance to the city gate.
What did Abimelech do after he captured the city?
Abimelech killed the people, tore down the city, and spread salt over it.
Where did the leaders of the tower of Shechem enter?
The leaders of the tower of Shechem entered the citadel of the house of El-Berith.
How did Abimelech kill all the leaders and people in the tower of Shechem?
Abimelech went up to Mount Zalmon, piled branches around the fortress and set it on fire, killing all the people in it.
When Abimelech came near the entrance of the tower of Thebez, what happened to him?
When Abimelech came near the entrance of the tower of Thebez, a woman on the roof dropped a millstone on his head and it crushed his skull.
Why did Abimelech tell his armor-bearer to draw his sword and kill him?
Abimelech told his armor-bearer to draw his sword and kill him so no one would say a women killed Abimelech.
Shamir was in the hill country of Ephraim.
Why did Yahweh burn with anger toward the people of Israel?
The people of Israel forsook Yahweh and no longer served him, so he became angry with Israel.
The Ammonites crossed over the Jordan to fight against the people of Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim, so that Israel was greatly distressed.
To whom did Yahweh tell the people of Israel to call out for help?
Yahweh told the people to call out to the gods that they had worshiped to show them that those gods could not save them.
Why could Yahweh no longer bear the misery of Israel?
Israel removed the foreign gods from their midst and they worshiped Yahweh, so he had compassion on them.
Jephthah was the son of a prostitute and Gilead.
Why did the elders of Gilead go to bring Jephthah back from the land of Tob?
The elders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah back from the land of Tob so he would be their commander in their fight against the Ammonites.
Why did the elders of Gilead come to Jephthah?
The elders of Gilead came to Jephthah because they wanted him to come with them to fight the Ammonites and be their leader.
If the elders of Gideon brought Jephthah home again to fight against the soldiers of Ammon, and if Yahweh gave them victory over them, what would happen to Jephthah?
If the elders of Gideon brought Jephthah home again to fight against the soldiers of Ammon, and if Yahweh gave them victory over them, Jephthah would be their leader.
Why did the people of Ammon come to fight to take the land of Israel?
The people of Ammon came to take the land of Israel because they claimed that when Israel came up out of Egypt, Israel seized the land of Ammon.
Who was not willing to let Israel pass?
The king of Edom and the king of Moab were not willing to let Israel pass.
Who gave Israel victory over Sihon?
Yahweh, the God of Israel, gave Israel victory over Sihon.
For how long did Israel live in Heshbon and its villages and in Aroer and its villages and in all the cities that are along the banks of the Arnon?
Israel lived for 300 years in Heshbon and Aroer and their villages as well as in all the cities that are along the banks of the Arnon.
If Yahweh gave Jephthah victory over the people of Ammon, what did Jephthah vow to do?
If Yahweh gave Jephthah victory over the people of Ammon, Jephthah would offer up as a burnt offering whoever came out of the doors of his house to greet him.
When Jephthah passed through to the people of Ammon to fight against them, who gave him the victory?
When Jephthah passed through to the people of Ammon to fight against them, Yahweh gave him victory.
How many children did Jephthah have?
Jephthah had only one child, this daughter.
What did Jephthah’s daughter want to do before he did everything he had promised?
She wanted him to leave her alone for two months, that she could go down to the hills and grieve over her virginity.
What did Jephthah do with his daughter?
He did what he had promised in the vow he had made.
What did the men of Ephraim want to do to Jephthah’s house because he did not call them to go with him?
The men of Ephraim wanted to burn Jephthah’s house down because he did not call them to go with him to fight against the people of Ammon.
Why did the men of Gilead attack the men of Ephraim?
The men of Gilead attacked the men of Ephraim because Ephraimites said the Gileadites were fugitives from Ephraim.
How did the men of Gilead test if a man was from Ephraim?

They would tell him to say “Shibboleth.” And if he said, “Sibboleth,” (for the Ephraimites could not pronounce the word correctly), the Gileadites would seize him and kill him at the fords of the Jordan.
Manoah was from the clan of Dan.
Why was no razor to come onto the child’s head?
No razor was to come onto his head, for the child was to be a Nazirite to God.
What did the man of God look like?
The man of God looked like an angel of God.
When the angel of God came a second time, who was there?
When the angel of God came a second time, only Manoah’s wife was there.
What did Manoah ask the angel about?
Manoah asked the angel about the rules for the boy and what his work would be.
If Manoah prepared a burnt offering, to whom was he to offer it?
If Manoah prepared a burnt offering, he was to offer it to Yahweh.
What wonderful thing did Yahweh do while Manoah and his wife were watching?
While Manoah and his wife were watching, the angel of Yahweh went up in the flame of the altar.
Where did Yahweh’s Spirit begin to stir Samson?
Yahweh’s Spirit began to stir Samson in Mahaneh Dan.
Who did Samson want his parents to get for him to be his wife?
Samson wanted his parents to get for him a woman in Timnah, one of the daughters of the Philistines, to be his wife.
Why did Samson want his parents to get him the woman in Timnah as his wife?
He wanted his parents to get him the woman in Timnah as his wife, for when he looked at her, she pleased him.
How was Samson able to tear the lion apart?
Yahweh’s Spirit suddenly came on him, and he tore the lion apart.
What was in the carcass of the lion?
There was a swarm of bees and honey in the carcass of the lion.
What would Samson get if the 30 companions could not answer his riddle?
Samson would get 30 linen robes and 30 changes of clothes if the 30 companions could not answer his riddle.
What would happen to Samson’s wife if she did not entice her husband to get the answer to the riddle?
If Samson’s wife did not entice her husband to get the answer to the riddle, the 30 companions would burn up her and her father’s house.
For how long did Samson’s wife cry in order to get the answer to the riddle?
She cried for the seven days that the feast lasted.
How did Samson get 30 changes of clothing?
Samson went down to Ashkelon and killed 30 men among those people and took their changes of clothing.
When Samson went to visit his wife, why did her father not allow him to go in?
The father thought Samson hated his wife, so had already given her to one of Samson’s companions.
How did Samson retaliate after finding out his wife had been given to another?
Samson retaliated by catching 300 foxes, tying torches to them, and letting them go in the Philistines’ grain.
When the Philistines were told that Samson burned their fields, what did they do?
When the Philistines were told that Samson burned their fields, they burned his wife and her father.
Why did Samson kill a great number of Philistines?
Samson killed a great number of Philistines to avenge the killing of his wife and her father.
Why did the Philistines come up to attack Judah?
The Philistines came up to attack Judah so they could capture Samson in order to kill him as he had killed so many of them.
When the men of Judah came to tie up Samson, what did he make them swear?
When the men of Judah came to tie up Samson, he made them swear that they would not kill him themselves.
With what did Samson kill 1,000 men?
Samson killed 1,000 men with a fresh jawbone of a donkey.
After Samson killed 1,000 men with a fresh jawbone of a donkey, how did he think he would die?
After Samson killed 1,000 men with a fresh jawbone of a donkey, he thought he would die of thirst.
God split open the hollow place at Lehi, and water came out.
When did the Gazites plan to kill Samson?
The Gazites planned to kill Samson at daylight.
Samson took hold of the city gate and its two posts, and he pulled them up out of the ground, bar and all.
If Delilah enticed Samson to tell her the secret of his strength, what would the leaders of the Philistines give her?
If Delilah enticed Samson to tell her the secret of his strength, each of the Philistine leaders would give her 1,100 pieces of silver.
When Delilah told Samson the Philistines were upon him, what did he do?
When Delilah told Samson the Philistines were upon him, he broke the cords with which he was tied.
When Samson tore off the new ropes from his arms, where were the men lying in wait?
When Samson tore off the new ropes from his arms, the men were waiting in one of the rooms of the house.
How much did Delilah beg Samson to tell her his secret?
She begged him so much that he wished he would die.
Why had Samson never cut the hair on his head?
Samson had never cut the hair on his head, for he had been a Nazirite of God from his mother’s womb.
How was Delilah able to subdue Samson?
Delilah was able to subdue him when the locks of his head were shaven off, for his strength left him.
What work did the Philistines make Samson do?
The Philistines made Samson turn the millstone to grind grain in the prison.
Why did the leaders of the Philistines gather together to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god?
The leaders of the Philistines had a celebration to offer sacrifices to Dagon their god because they said he had conquered Samson.
Who helped Samson touch the columns on which the building rested?
The young man leading Samson by the hand led him so he could touch the columns which supported the building.
Why did Samson want God to strengthen him?
Samson wanted God to strengthen him so that he could have revenge in one blow on the Philistines for taking his two eyes.
How many people did Samson kill when the building fell?
Samson killed more at his death than those he had killed during his life.
Micah stole 1,100 pieces of silver from his mother.
For what did Micah’s mother set apart the silver?
Micah’s mother said she had dedicated the silver to Yahweh, for her son to make an idol.
To what did Micah appoint one of his sons?
He appointed one of his sons to become his priest.
Why did the Levite leave Bethlehem?
The Levite left Bethlehem to go and find a place to live.
What did Micah ask the Levite to be to him?
Micah asked the Levite to live with him and be an adviser and a priest to him.
Why did Micah think Yahweh would be good to him?
Micah thought Yahweh would be good to him because he had a Levite as his priest.
Why were the descendants of Dan looking for a territory in which to live?
The descendants of Dan were looking for a territory in which to live because they had not been able to occupy all of the territory that had been assigned to them.
What did the people of Dan want the Levite to ask God?
The people of Dan wanted the Levite to ask God if they would succeed in what they were trying to do.
What did the five men from Dan want to do with the land of Laish?
The five men from Dan wanted to take possession of the land so their people could live there.
What did the five men say was in the houses of Laish?
The five men said that in the houses of Laish there were a sacred vest, household idols, and a silver molded figure.
Micah was angry because the Danites stole the idols he had made and his priest and they were leaving.
Why did Micah turn and go back to his house?
When Micah saw that they were too strong for him, he turned and went back to his house.
Why was there no one to rescue the people of Laish?
There was no one to rescue the people of Laish because it was a long way from Sidon and they had no other allies.
Who were the priests for the tribe of the Danites?
Jonathan, the son of Gershom, (the grandson of Moses) and his sons were priests for the tribe of Dan.
The Levite was living in a remote area of the hill country of Ephraim.
Where did the Levite’s concubine bring him?
The concubine brought the Levite into the house of her father.
Although the Levite intended to go home, what did his father-in-law want him to do?
His father-in-law wanted him to stay and spend the night.
What did the Levite’s father-in-law ask him to do again on the fifth day?
His father-in-law asked him to stay another night and have a good time.
Why did the Levite not want to spend the night in Jebus?
The Levite did not want to stay in a city where there were no other Israelites.
Why did the Levite and his servant sit down in the city square?
They sat down in the city square, for no one had offered them a place to stay for the night.
From what tribe were the men living in Gibeah?
The men living in Gibeah were from the tribe of Benjamin.
What did the old man warn the Levite not to do?
The old man warned the Levite not to spend the night in the open square.
Why did the wicked men of the city want the old man to bring out the man who was staying in his house?
The wicked men of the city wanted the old man to bring out the man who came was staying in his house so they could have sex with him.
Who did the old man offer to the wicked men in place of the Levite?
The old man offered them his virgin daughter and the Levite’s concubine.
At dawn the wicked men let the concubine go. She came and she fell down at the door of the man’s house where her master was, and she lay there until it was light.
What did the Levite do when his concubine did not answer him?
When the Levite’s concubine did not answer him, he put her body on the donkey and set out for home.
What did the Levite do to his concubine’s body?
The Levite cut her up into twelve pieces and sent the pieces to each of the tribes throughout Israel.
Who gathered together before Yahweh at Mizpah?
All the people from Dan to Beersheba, including the land of Gilead, gathered together before Yahweh at Mizpah.
What did the Levite say the men of Gibeah did to him?
The Levite said the men of Gibeah surrounded the house in order to abuse and kill him.
Why did the tribes of Israel tell Benjamin to give them those wicked men of Gibeah?
The tribes of Israel told Benjamin to give them those wicked men of Gibeah, so they might put them to death in order to completely remove this evil from Israel.
Why did the people of Benjamin come together at Gibeah?
The people of Benjamin came together at Gibeah to defend it against the people of Israel.
What was special about the 700 chosen men?
The 700 chosen men were left-handed; each of them could sling a stone with great accuracy.
The people asked God and he told them that Judah should attack first.
After Benjamin killed many soldiers of Israel, what did the soldiers of Israel do?
After Benjamin killed many soldiers of Israel, the soldiers of Israel wept and fasted before Yahweh until evening. They also offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to Yahweh.
Where was the Box of the Covenant of God in those days?
The Box of the Covenant of God was in Bethel at that time.
When the soldiers of Israel drew away from the city, what did the people of Benjamin think?
When the soldiers of Israel drew away from the city, the people of Benjamin thought they had defeated them and they were running away.
Why had the men of Israel retreated?
The men of Israel had retreated because they wanted the Benjaminites to be drawn out of the city where they had men hidden outside Gibeah waiting to attack them.
What was the signal between the soldiers of Israel and the men hiding in secret?
The arranged signal between the soldiers of Israel and the men hiding in secret was that a great cloud of smoke would rise up out of the city.
Why could the men of Benjamin not escape?
The men of Benjamin ran away from the soldiers of Israel, trying to escape into the wilderness, but they were caught between the two groups of Israelites.
How many soldiers of Benjamin turned and fled to the wilderness?
Six hundred men were able to escape to the wilderness.
Why did the men of Israel say that one of their tribes might not exist anymore?

The men of Israel worried that the Benjaminite tribe would no longer exist since they had promised to not allow their daughters to marry a Benjaminite so the remaining men would not have women to marry.
Who would certainly be put to death?
Anyone who did not come when they met with Yahweh at Mizpah would certainly be put to death.
Which of the cities did not come to meet with Yahweh at Mizpah?
No one from the city of Jabesh Gilead had come to meet with Yahweh at Mizpah.
Who did the men take from those living in Jabesh Gilead?
The men took 400 young women who had never slept with a man from those living in Jabesh Gilead.
What was the problem when the Benjaminites were given the women of Jabesh Gilead?
When the Benjaminites were given the women of Jabesh Gilead, there were not enough women for all of them to marry.
Shiloh was north of Bethel, east of the road that went up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.
When were the Benjaminites to each rush out of the vineyards and grab a wife from the young women of Shiloh?
When the young women from Shiloh came out to dance, each Benjaminite was to rush out of the vineyards and grab a young woman as his wife.
Why would the men of Shiloh not be guilty of breaking their oath?
The men of Shiloh were told that they had not broken their oath since they had not given their daughters to the Benjaminites as wives but instead, the young women had been stolen.
How did everyone live in those days when Israel had no king?
Everyone did what he thought was right in his own eyes.
During what period of time in Jewish history did the story of Ruth occur?
It occurred in the days when the judges ruled.
Why did Elimelek move to Moab with his family?
He moved because there was a famine in the land of Judah.
What happened to Elimelek in Moab?
He died, leaving Naomi a widow.
What happened to Naomi’s children in Moab?
They died, leaving behind two daughters-in-law for Naomi.
Why did Naomi decide to return to Judah?
She heard that Yahweh had given the people of Judah food.
Where did Naomi want her two daughters-in-law to go?
She wanted them to return to their mothers’ houses.
What did Naomi want her two daughters-in-law to find?
She wanted them to find other husbands.
Who did Naomi believe was the source of her trouble?
She believed that Yahweh was against her.
When Ruth stayed with Naomi, what promise did Ruth make to Naomi?
She said, “For I will go to the place where you go, and I will stay in the place where you stay. Your people are my people, and your God is my God.”
How long did Ruth say she would remain with Naomi?

She said she would remain with Naomi until they died. She said, “In the place where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May Yahweh do thus to me, and thus may he add, if death separates between me and between you.”
To which town did Naomi return?
What name did Naomi want to be called and why?
She asked to be called “Mara” (which means “bitter”), because she believed that Yahweh had dealt bitterly with her.
What time of the year did Naomi and Ruth arrive in Bethlehem?
They arrived at the beginning of the barley harvest.
What was the relationship between Boaz and Naomi’s dead husband?
Boaz was a relative of Naomi’s husband.
As Ruth went out to glean for the first time, who did Ruth say she would follow while gleaning grain?
She would follow anyone in whose eyes she found favor.
What greeting did Boaz give to his workers?
What did Boaz want to know about Ruth?
He wanted to know to whom she belonged.
What instructions did Boaz give Ruth concerning her gleaning?
He told Ruth not to leave his field, but to stay and work in his field with his female workers.
After receiving the favorable instructions, what question did Ruth ask Boaz?
She asked Boaz why she had found favor in his sight.
What good report had Boaz heard about Ruth?
He had heard that Ruth had left her home to follow Naomi.
Under whose wings did Boaz say Ruth had found refuge?
He said that Ruth had found refuge under Yahweh’s wings.
What additional favor did Boaz show to Ruth when they returned to work after mealtime?
He allowed Ruth to glean among the bundles.
What did Boaz tell his workers to do for Ruth?
He commanded the reapers to pull out grain for Ruth from the bundles.
When Naomi saw the large amount of grain that Ruth brought back, what question did she ask Ruth?
She asked where Ruth had gleaned that day.
What blessing did Naomi wish for Boaz when she heard that Boaz had helped Ruth?
She said, “May he be blessed by Yahweh.”
Why did Naomi think it was good for Ruth to work with Boaz’s women workers?
By doing that, Ruth would not come to harm in any other field.
What did Ruth do during the rest of the barley harvest?
She gleaned with Boaz’s workers and lived with her mother-in-law.
What did Naomi say her desire was for Ruth?
She desired that Ruth have a place of rest, meaning to have a person who would treat her well.
What did Naomi tell Ruth to do before going down to the threshing floor?
She told her to wash and anoint herself and to put on her cloak.
What was Ruth to do when she went to where Boaz was sleeping?
She was to uncover his feet and to lie down there.
What was Ruth’s attitude toward Naomi’s instructions?
She said she would do everything Naomi told her to do.
At midnight, what was Boaz startled to find?
He was startled to find that a woman lay at his feet!
What was Ruth’s request to Boaz?
She asked Boaz to spread his cloak over her, for he was a kinsman-redeemer.
Why did Boaz ask a blessing from Yahweh for Ruth?
Boaz blessed Ruth because she had come to Boaz, her kinsman-redeemer, rather than pursuing younger men.
What did Boaz say he would do about Ruth’s request?
He said that he would do all that she asked.
What obstacle prevented Boaz from immediately performing the part of a kinsman for Ruth?
There was another kinsman-redeemer nearer in relationship than Boaz.
How was Boaz going to determine who would act as kinsman for Ruth?
If the nearest kinsman-redeemer was willing to redeem Ruth, then Boaz would let him do that. But if he was not willing, then Boaz would be the kinsman-redeemer.
Why did Ruth leave the threshing floor early before anyone could recognize her?
Boaz did not want people to know that she had been with him overnight at the threshing floor.
What gift did Boaz give Ruth before she left the threshing floor?
He gave her six large measures of barley.
Naomi was sure that Boaz would resolve the issue by what time?
He would resolve it by the end of that same day.
Where did Boaz go to resolve the issue of who would be the kinsman-redeemer for Ruth?
He went to the gate of the city.
Who did Boaz ask to sit as witnesses?
He asked ten men who were from the elders of the city.
What did Boaz first speak about to the other kinsman?
He told him that Naomi was selling the piece of land that had been owned by Elimelek.
What did Boaz suggest the other kinsman do about the parcel of land?
Boaz suggested that the other kinsman could redeem it.
What was the other kinsman’s answer?
He said he would redeem it.
About what additional requirement did Boaz then tell the other kinsman?
He told him that he would also have to marry Ruth in order to raise up the name of the dead man over his inheritance.
What was the other kinsman’s answer when he learned that he would have to marry Ruth?
He said he could not redeem the land.
Why did the other kinsman say he could not be the redeemer?
He said that it would damage his own inheritance.
What did the other kinsman do to show that he agreed that Boaz should be the redeemer?
He took off his sandal and gave it to him in front of witnesses.
What was the first agreement that Boaz said the elders witnessed?
They witnessed that Boaz bought all the land that had belonged to Elimelek.
What was the second agreement that Boaz said the elders had witnessed?
They had witnessed that Boaz acquired Ruth as his wife.
What blessing did the people desire for Boaz?
They desired that Yahweh would give him offspring through Ruth, just as Tamar bore a son to Judah.
Why did the women say that Ruth was better for Naomi than seven sons?
They said this because of Ruth’s love for Naomi, and because Ruth had given birth to a grandson for Naomi.
What was Naomi’s relationship with Ruth’s son?
Naomi became his nurse or caregiver.
Of whom was Obed the father and grandfather?
Obed was the father of Jesse and the grandfather of David.
Who were the two wives of Elkanah?
The wives of Elkanah were Hannah and Peninnah.
How many children did Hannah have at that time?
At that time Hannah had no children.
Why did Elkanah give twice as much meat to Hannah?
He gave a double portion to Hannah because he loved her.
Why did Hannah’s adversary provoke her?
She provoked Hannah in order to make her upset, because Yahweh had closed her womb.
What did Hannah do because she was so sorrowful about not having children?
She went to the house of Yahweh, and she cried very sorrowfully as she prayed to Yahweh.
What did Hannah vow to Yahweh?
Hannah vowed that if Yahweh would give her a son, she would give him to Yahweh and they would never cut his hair.
Because Hannah was speaking to Yahweh from her heart, what did Eli the priest think about her actions?
Eli saw Hannah’s lips moving but did not hear her voice, so he thought she was drunk.
What did Hannah assure Eli she was doing?
Hannah assured Eli that she was not drunk but was talking to Yahweh because someone made her feel very badly.
What did Eli say to Hannah that caused her to go on her way, eat, and no longer feel sad?
Eli told her to go in peace and said that he hoped the God of Israel would grant her request.
When Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son, what did she name him?
Hannah named her son Samuel because she had requested him from Yahweh.
Why did Hannah not go with her husband to the house of Yahweh for the yearly sacrifice?
She did not go because she was waiting until her son was weaned.
What offerings did Hannah bring with her when she brought her son to the house of Yahweh?
Hannah brought three bulls, an ephah of flour, and a skin of wine.
What did Hannah present to Yahweh?
Hannah presented her son to Yahweh for as long as he would live.
Why did Hannah laugh at her enemies?
Hannah laughed because she rejoiced in Yahweh’s salvation.
Why does Hannah say that people should not boast or speak arrogantly?
People should not boast or speak arrogantly because Yahweh is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.
In Hannah’s song, who is the one who is unable to have more children?
The woman who had many children before is not able to have any more.
Who decides death and life, or who goes down to Sheol or is raised up?
Yahweh is the one who decides death and life, and who causes people to go down to Sheol or to come up from there.
Who makes people poor or rich?
Yahweh makes people poor, and he makes them rich.
Who raises up the poor and lifts the needy to sit in a seat of honor?
Yahweh raises them up to sit in a seat of honor.
Who does Hannah say will protect the feet of his faithful people and silence the wicked in darkness?
Hannah says that Yahweh will guard the feet of his faithful people and will silence the wicked.
Who will judge the ends of the earth and give strength to his king?
Yahweh will judge the ends of the earth and give strength to his king.
What child served Yahweh in the presence of Eli the priest?
Samuel served Yahweh in the presence of Eli the priest.
Whose sons were wicked men who did not know Yahweh?
Eli the priest’s sons did very bad things.
What was the custom of the priests with the people at the time of sacrifice?
The custom was for the priest’s servant to come with a three-pronged fork while the meat was boiling and take whatever the fork brought up for the priest.
What evil thing did Eli’s sons have their servant do?
They had their servant demand raw meat for the priest before the fat was burned as an offering to Yahweh, and had him take it by force if the person refused.
Why was the sin of Eli’s sons so great?
Their sin was great before Yahweh because the men were treating very disrespectfully the offerings that people were bringing to Yahweh.
What would Samuel’s mother make for him from year to year to clothe him?
She would make him a small robe each year.
How would Eli bless Elkanah and his wife?
Eli blessed them by asking Yahweh to give them more children from Hannah.
What was Yahweh’s response to Eli’s prayer for Samuel’s parents to have more children?
Yahweh helped Hannah, and she bore three more sons and two daughters.
What did Eli say to his sons when he heard evil reports about them?
Eli told his sons that the report he was hearing from Yahweh’s people about their evil deeds was not good. He told them to stop doing what they were doing.
Why did Eli’s sons not listen to his voice?
Eli’s sons did not listen to his voice because Yahweh desired to make them die.
Who grew up and was good in the sight of Yahweh and also with men?
Samuel grew up and was good in the sight of Yahweh and with men.
Who told Eli that Yahweh chose Eli’s ancestors out of all the tribes of Israel to be Yahweh’s priest?
A man of God told Eli that Yahweh had chosen his ancestors.
How had Eli and his sons scorned Yahweh’s sacrifices and offerings?
They scorned the sacrifices and offerings by honoring his sons above Yahweh and fattening themselves on the best parts of offerings.
What did Yahweh tell Eli would happen to the men in his family?
Yahweh told Eli that all the men born in his family would die young.
What did Yahweh say would be a sign to Eli that his prophecy would come true?
The sign would be that both of his sons would die on the same day.
Who will walk before Yahweh’s faithful priest always?
Yahweh has chosen another man who will serve him faithfully and continually be a helper to the king whom Yahweh will appoint.
Why will everyone left in Eli’s family come and bow down to the faithful priest?
They will ask him to allow them to work with the other priests so that they can have food to eat.
What was Samuel’s reply when he heard Yahweh call to him as he was lying down?
Samuel replied that he was ready to do whatever you ask.
What did Eli tell Samuel to do when Samuel ran to him?
Eli said that he did not call Samuel and told him to go lie down again.
What had not yet been revealed to Samuel?
The word of Yahweh had not yet been revealed to Samuel.
What did Eli realize after the third time that Samuel came to him?
Eli realized that it was Yahweh who had been calling Samuel.
What did Eli tell Samuel to say if he was called again?
Eli told Samuel to say that Yahweh should speak, because his servant was listening.
What did Yahweh say would happen to the ears of everyone when they heard what he was going to do?
Yahweh said that the ears of everyone who heard it would tingle.
What had Eli’s sons brought upon themselves?
Eli’s sons had brought a curse upon themselves.
What would never be atoned for by sacrifice or offering?
The iniquity of Eli’s house would never be atoned for by sacrifice or offering.
What was Samuel afraid to do in the morning after he opened the doors of the house of Yahweh?
He was afraid to tell Eli about the vision.
What did Samuel do after Eli told him that he must not hide from him the words that Yahweh had spoken?
Samuel told him everything and hid nothing from him.
What did all Israel from Dan to Beersheba know about Samuel?
All Israel knew that Samuel was established as a prophet of Yahweh.
What was the result of the battle between Israel and the Philistines?
Israel was defeated by the Philistines.
What did the elders of Israel decide to do so that they could be saved from the power of their enemies?
The elders decided to bring the Box of the Covenant of Yahweh from Shiloh to be with them.
Who was with the Box of the Covenant of God?
The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the Box of the Covenant.
What did the Philistines wonder when they heard the great shout from the people of Israel?
The Philistines wondered about the meaning of the great shout in the camp of the Hebrews.
Who did the Philistines say had come into the camp of the Hebrews?
The Philistines said that a god had come into the camp.
With what did the Philistines say that the gods of Israel had struck the Egyptians in the wilderness?
They said that the gods had struck the Egyptians with every kind of plague.
What happened to the two sons of Eli when the Box of God was taken Israel was struck and fled?
The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, died.
What did the whole city do when the man from the battle line entered the city and told the news?
When the man told the news, the whole city cried out.
What question did Eli ask when he heard the noise of the outcry?
Eli asked what the sound of the tumult meant.
What did the man tell Eli had happened to his sons and to the Box of God when Israel was defeated?
The man told Eli that his two sons were dead and the Box of God had been taken.
What was the injury that killed Eli when he fell over backward from his seat by the side of the gate?
Eli broke his neck and he died.
What happened when Phinehas’s pregnant wife heard that the Box of God was captured and her father-in-law and husband were dead?
Phinehas’s wife knelt down and gave birth because her labor pains suddenly began.
What name did Phinehas’s wife give to the baby and why did she give him that name?
She named the baby Ichabod, saying that the glory had departed from Israel because the Box of God had been taken.
In what position did the people find the idol Dagon the next day after the Philistines brought the Box of God into Dagon’s house?
Dagon was found fallen face down on the ground before the Box of Yahweh.
What remained of the idol Dagon the next morning after they had set him back in his place?
Only the body of Dagon remained; his head and hands were lying cut off in the doorway.
Why did the men of Ashdod say that the Box of the God of Israel should not stay with them?
They said it should not stay because the hand of their God was severe against them and against their god Dagon.
To what place did the Philistines move the Box of the God of Israel?
The Philistines moved the Box to Gath.
With what did Yahweh strike the men of the city of Gath?
What did the people of Ekron say the Box of the God of Israel would do to them?
They said that it would kill them and their people.
To what place did the people of Ekron ask the rulers to send the Box?
They asked that the Box be sent back to its own place.
To what place did the cry of the city go?
The cry of the city went up to the heavens.
For how long was the Box of Yahweh in the Philistines’ country?
The Box was in the country of the Philistines for seven months.
Who did the Philistines call to ask for advice on how the Box of Yahweh should be sent back to its own country?
They called for the priests and the diviners to tell them how to send the Box back.
What did the priests and diviners tell the Philistine people to send as a guilt offering to the God of Israel?
They told the Philistines to send five gold tumors and five gold mice.
Why did the priests and diviners say the people should not be stubborn like the Egyptians and Pharaoh were?
Because when God dealt severely with the Egyptians and Pharaoh, they had to let Israel go.
What animals did the priests and diviners tell the Philistines to tie to the cart for the Box of Yahweh?
They told the Philistines to hitch two nursing cows to the cart.
How would the Philistines know that it was Yahweh who had done this great harm to them?
The Philistines would know it was Yahweh if the cows pulling the cart went on their own to Beth Shemesh.
Where did the nursing cows go with the cart carrying the Box and the gold mice and tumors?
The cows went straight in the direction of Beth Shemesh.
What were the people of Beth Shemesh doing when they lifted up their eyes and saw the Box?
They were harvesting their wheat in the valley.
What did the people of Beth Shemesh do with the cows that had pulled the cart?
They offered the cows as a burnt offering to Yahweh.
Who took down the Box of Yahweh and the box that was with it?
The Levites took down the Box of Yahweh and the box that was with it.
What did the five rulers of the Philistines do when they saw what had happened?
They returned that day to Ekron.
What did the numbers of gold tumors and gold mice represent?
The five gold tumors represented the people of their five cities, and the gold mice represented all the Philistine cities belonging to those rulers.
Why did Yahweh strike some of the men of Beth Shemesh?
Yahweh struck them because they looked into his Box.
What did the messengers from Beth Shemesh ask the people of Kiriath Jearim to do?
The messengers asked the people of Kiriath Jearim to come and take the Box of Yahweh to their city.
What did the men of Kiriath Jearim do to Abinadab’s son, Eleazar, so that he could take care of the Box of Yahweh?
They consecrated him to keep the Box of Yahweh.
What did all the house of Israel do during the twenty years that the Box remained in Kiriath Jearim?
During that time, the Israelite people were very sorry that Yahweh was not helping them anymore.
What did Samuel tell the people of Israel that they needed to remove from among them for Yahweh to rescue them from the Philistines?
Samuel told them that they needed to remove the foreign gods and the Ashtoreths from among them and serve Yahweh only.
What did the people of Israel admit that they had done when they gathered at Mizpah?
They admitted that they had sinned against Yahweh.
Why did the people of Israel ask Samuel to call out to Yahweh for them?
They were afraid because they heard that the rulers of the Philistines were coming to attack them.
What did Yahweh do when Samuel offered a lamb as a burnt offering and cried out to him?
What did Yahweh do that threw the Philistines into confusion as they drew near to attack Israel?
Yahweh thundered with a great sound on that day against the Philistines.
What did Samuel set up between Mizpah and Shen as a remembrance that Yahweh had helped them?
Samuel took a stone and set it up.
What happened to the towns that the Philistines had taken from Israel?
What did Samuel do as he went on a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, Mizpah, and back to Ramah?
Samuel judged Israel in all these places.
In what ways did Samuel’s two sons, who were judges, not walk in the ways of their father?
They were not honest like their father. They accepted bribes, and they did not make honest decisions about people’s disputes.
What request did the elders of Israel make of Samuel?
They asked Samuel to appoint a king to judge them, like all the other nations.
What did Samuel do when he was displeased by the elders’ request to give them a king?
Why did Yahweh tell Samuel to listen to the voice of the people?
Yahweh told Samuel to listen because the people were not rejecting Samuel, but they were rejecting Yahweh from reigning over them.
What warning did Yahweh tell Samuel to give to the people of Israel?
Yahweh told Samuel to warn the people about the way the king would rule over them.
For what did Samuel warn the people that a king would take their sons?
Samuel warned that the king would take their sons to be officers and soldiers, to plow his fields and harvest his crops, and to make weapons of war.
How did Samuel warn the people about what a king would do with their daughters and property?
Samuel warned that the king would take their daughters to be perfumers, cooks, and bakers, and he would take the best of their fields and vineyards and olive groves to give to his attendants.
How did Samuel warn the people about what a king would do with their servants and animals?
Samuel warned that the king would take their servants, the best of their young men and donkeys, and a tenth of their flocks, and the people would become his servants.
What did Samuel warn would happen when the people cried out because of the king they had chosen?
Samuel said that Yahweh would not answer them on that day.
How did the people of Israel respond to the warnings from Samuel?
The people refused to listen and said they wanted a king over them so they could be like the other nations.
What was Yahweh’s response when Samuel repeated the people’s words to him?
Yahweh told Samuel to listen to their voice and appoint a king for them.
What were the outstanding physical features of Saul, the son of Kish?
Saul was a handsome young man who was taller than any of the other people from his shoulders upward.
What was the outcome when Kish asked his son Saul to go and look for their lost donkeys?
Saul took one of the servants and passed through many places without finding them.
What did Saul tell his servant they should do when they came to the land of Zuph?
Saul told his servant that they should go back so his father would not stop being concerned about the donkeys and become concerned about them.
What different idea did the servant present to Saul?
The servant suggested they should go to a man of God in the city who might tell them the way they should go.
What did the servant have to give to the man of God so he would tell them which way to go?
The servant had a fourth of a shekel of silver to give to the man of God.
What did Saul and his servant ask the young women who were coming out to draw water?
Saul and his servant asked if the seer was in the city.
Why was the seer coming to the city on that day?
The seer was coming to the city because the people were having a sacrifice at the high place, and he would bless the sacrifice.
What did Yahweh reveal to Samuel about Saul’s role in Israel?
Yahweh told Samuel that he was to anoint Saul as ruler over Israel, and Saul would save Yahweh’s people from the hand of the Philistines.
What invitation did Samuel give to Saul after he revealed that he was the seer Saul was seeking?
Samuel invited Saul to go up and eat with him at the high place.
How did Samuel surprise Saul with what he told him?
Samuel told him that all the desire of Israel was for him and his father’s house, even though Saul was from the least clan of the smallest tribe.
What did Samuel tell the cook to serve to Saul?
Samuel told the cook to serve Saul the thigh portion that had been set aside for him for the appointed time.
What did Samuel say to Saul from the roof in the morning?
Samuel told Saul to get up so he could send him on his way.
Why did Samuel tell Saul to stand still for a while on the outskirts of the city?
Samuel told Saul to stand still so Samuel could tell him the word of God.
Why did Samuel pour a flask of oil on Saul’s head and kiss him?
He did this because Yahweh had anointed Saul to be a ruler over his inheritance.
What future event did Samuel share with Saul?
Samuel told Saul that he would find two men near Rachel’s tomb who would tell him that the donkeys had been found.
What did Samuel tell Saul would happen when he came to the oak of Tabor?
Three men going up to God at Bethel would meet him and give him two loaves of bread, which he should take.
What did Samuel tell Saul would happen when he came to Gibeah of God?
The Spirit of Yahweh would rush upon him, he would prophesy with a group of prophets, and he would be changed into a different man.
What instructions did Samuel give to Saul for later?
Samuel told Saul to go down to Gilgal and wait seven days for Samuel to come and offer sacrifices.
What happened when Saul turned his back to leave Samuel?
When Saul turned to leave, God changed Saul’s inner being.
Why did people wonder if Saul was one of the prophets?
They saw him prophesying with the prophets and wondered how this had happened to the son of Kish.
What did Saul tell his uncle when he was asked where he had gone?
Saul told his uncle that when he and his servant could not find the donkeys, they went to Samuel.
What did Saul not tell his uncle about what Samuel had said to him?
Saul did not tell his uncle about the matter of the kingship.
Why did Yahweh say that Israel had rejected him?
Israel had rejected Yahweh because they had asked for a king to be set over them.
What happened when Saul, the son of Kish, was chosen as the next king?
They looked for Saul, but he could not be found.
Where was Saul when he was chosen as the next king?
Saul had hidden himself among the bags.
What did Samuel say about the man whom Yahweh had chosen?
Samuel said that there was no one like Saul among all the people.
How were the customs of the kingship established and preserved?
Samuel told the people the customs of the kingship, wrote them in a book, and placed the book before Yahweh.
How did some wicked men show their dislike for Saul?
Some wicked men despised Saul and did not bring him a gift.
What was the response of Nahash the Ammonite to the request for a covenant from the men of Jabesh?
He said he would make a covenant with them if he could gouge out all their right eyes and bring disgrace on Israel.
How did the elders of Jabesh respond to Nahash’s proposal?
They asked for seven days to send messengers throughout Israel to see if anyone would save them.
Why were the people in Saul’s town of Gibeah weeping?
They were weeping because they had heard the words of the men from Jabesh.
How did Saul respond to the threat against Jabesh?
The Spirit of God rushed upon him, he became very angry, and he persuaded the men of Israel and Judah to fight.
What message did the messengers bring back to the men of Jabesh?
They told the men of Jabesh that they would have deliverance the next day by the time the sun was hot.
What did the men of Jabesh say to Nahash the Ammonite?
They told Nahash that they would come out to him the next day, and he could do to them whatever seemed good to him.
What was the outcome of the battle between Israel and the Ammonites?
The people of Israel attacked and defeated the Ammonites, and the survivors were totally scattered.
Why did Saul say that none of the men who opposed him would be put to death?
Saul said no one would be put to death, because that day Yahweh had brought deliverance to Israel.
Why did Samuel, Saul, and all the people of Israel go to Gilgal?
They went to Gilgal to renew the kingship, make Saul king before Yahweh, and sacrifice peace offerings.
What did the people of Israel say when Samuel asked if he had ever wronged them?
The people of Israel told Samuel he had not defrauded or oppressed them or taken anything from anyone.
Why did Samuel tell the people of Israel to present themselves before Yahweh?
He told them to present themselves so he could make the case against them that they should not have asked for a king instead of trusting Yahweh to rescue them.
What did God do to the ancestors of Israel after they forgot Yahweh their God?
Yahweh sold them into the hand of Sisera, the Philistines, and the king of Moab, who all fought against them.
What did Yahweh do after Israel’s ancestors cried out to him and asked to be rescued from their enemies?
Yahweh sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue them.
What did Samuel remind the people of Israel that they had requested?
Samuel reminded the people that they had wanted a king to reign over them, even though Yahweh their God was their king.
What choice did Samuel present to the people of Israel?
They could fear Yahweh and serve him, or they could rebel against his command and his hand would be against them.
What did Samuel challenge the people of Israel to do?
Samuel challenged the people to stand and see the great thing Yahweh is doing before their eyes.
What did Samuel ask Yahweh to send so that the people would know the extent of their wickedness?
He asked Yahweh to send thunder and rain during the wheat harvest.
How did Samuel respond when the people of Israel realized their sin?
Samuel told the people not to be afraid, but to serve Yahweh with all their heart and not turn aside.
What message of comfort did Samuel give to the people of Israel?
Samuel comforted the people by telling them that Yahweh would not forsake them, because of his great name.
What did Samuel promise to do for Israel?
He promised to continue to pray for them and to instruct them in the good and right way.
What did Samuel challenge the people of Israel to do?
Samuel told them to fear Yahweh and serve him faithfully with all their heart, considering the great things he had done for them.
What did Saul do with the soldiers he did not choose to be with him?
Saul sent the rest of the soldiers home to their own tents.
How did Israel make itself stink among the Philistines?
They made themselves stink among the Philistines because Jonathan had struck the garrison of the Philistines at Geba.
How did the Philistines respond to the attack by Jonathan?
They gathered 30,000 chariots, 6,000 horsemen, and people as numerous as the sand on the seashore to fight against Israel.
How did the men of Israel react to the forces of the Philistines?
They were distressed, so they hid in caves, thickets, cliffs, pits, and cisterns, and some fled across the Jordan.
What did Saul do when Samuel did not come to Gilgal after seven days?
Saul offered the burnt offering himself.
What excuse did Saul give Samuel for not waiting for him to offer the sacrifices?
He said he saw that the Philistine army was going to attack, and he had not yet asked Yahweh to help Israel, so he forced himself to offer the burnt offering.
What did Samuel say would be the consequences of Saul’s disobedience?

Because Saul did not obey Yahweh’s command, none of his descendants will become king. Instead, Yahweh has found someone else who will do what he wants him to do, and he will make that person the next king of Israel.
Samuel told Saul that he had acted foolishly by not keeping the command that Yahweh gave him.
What strategy did the Philistines use against the people of Israel?
The Philistines sent out soldiers in three groups to attack different Israelite towns.
What problem did the Israelites face in their fight against the Philistines?
There were no blacksmiths in all the land of Israel, so they could not make swords or spears.
How were the soldiers of Israel hindered on the day of battle?
None of the people with Saul and Jonathan had a sword or spear in their hand.
What secret plan did Jonathan, the son of Saul, have?
Jonathan planned to cross over to the Philistines’ garrison, but he did not tell his father.
What did the six hundred men with Saul not know?
They did not know that Jonathan had gone.
What proposal did Jonathan present to his young armor-bearer?
Jonathan proposed that they cross over to the garrison of the uncircumcised, because perhaps Yahweh would act for them.
What was the armor-bearer’s response to the proposal?
Jonathan’s armor-bearer told him to do all that was in his heart and that he was with him and would help him in all that he wanted to do.
What would be the sign to Jonathan and his armor-bearer that Yahweh had given the Philistines into their hand?
If the Philistines told them to come up to them, that would be the sign.
What did Jonathan say to his armor-bearer after the Philistines told them to come up?
He told his armor-bearer to follow him because Yahweh had given the Philistines into the hand of Israel.
What was the result of the attack that Jonathan and his armor-bearer made on the Philistine garrison?
Jonathan and his armor-bearer killed about twenty men.
What did Saul do when his watchmen saw the Philistine army dispersing?
Saul had the people counted to see who was missing, and they discovered it was Jonathan and his armor-bearer.
Why did Saul tell Ahijah the priest to bring the Box of God to him?
Saul wanted to inquire of God, but he stopped because the tumult in the Philistine camp was increasing.
Who rejoined the Israelites who had remained with Saul and Jonathan?

The Hebrews who had previously deserted to the Philistines in their camp rejoined the Israelites. Now those men helped Saul and Jonathan and the other Israelite soldiers fight against the Philistines.
What caused the men of Israel to be distressed and faint?
Saul had put the people under an oath, cursing any man who ate food before evening.
How did Jonathan unknowingly break the oath?
Jonathan, who had not heard the oath, ate some honey from a honeycomb.
How was Jonathan critical of the oath his father had made?
Jonathan said that if the people had been allowed to eat from the plunder of their enemies, the slaughter among the Philistines would have been greater.
How did the people of Israel sin against Yahweh after their battle against the Philistines?
The people ate meat with the blood still in it.
What did Saul believe was the reason why he did not receive an answer when he inquired of God?
Saul believed that God did not answer him on that day because someone had sinned.
How did Saul say he would deal with the sin that had been committed?
He said that the person who committed the sin would surely die, even if it was his son Jonathan.
How was it determined that Jonathan was the person who had sinned?
The priest threw a lot, and it indicated that either Jonathan or Saul had sinned, not one of the other Israelite soldiers. He threw the lot again, and the lot indicated that Jonathan had sinned.
How was Jonathan saved from death?
The people redeemed Jonathan and would not allow him to die because he had brought about a great salvation for Israel.
How did Saul lead Israel as their king?
Saul fought against all his enemies on every side and rescued Israel from the hands of those who plundered them.
Why did Yahweh want Saul to attack and completely destroy Amalek?
Yahweh wanted to punish Amalek for what he had done to Israel when he opposed them on the way up from Egypt.
Why did Saul tell the Kenites to depart from the Amalekites?
He warned the Kenites to move away because they had shown kindness to the people of Israel when they came up from Egypt. He did not want to kill them when he killed the Amalekites.
How did Saul disobey the directions that Yahweh had given to him?
Saul spared King Agag and the best of the sheep, cattle, and lambs, and was not willing to devote them to destruction as Yahweh had commanded.
Why did Yahweh regret that he had made Saul king?
Yahweh regretted making Saul king because Saul had turned from following him and was no longer obedient to him.
What lie did Saul tell Samuel?
Saul told Samuel that he had obeyed what Yahweh told him to do.
How did Samuel respond to the lie that Saul had told him?
Samuel asked about the bleating of sheep and the lowing of cattle that he was hearing.
What excuse did Saul give to Samuel to explain his disobedience?
He said the people had spared the best of the sheep and cattle so they could sacrifice them to Yahweh.
He told Saul that Yahweh had sent him to devote the sinners, the Amalekites, to destruction, but instead he had swooped down on the plunder and done evil.
What excuse did Saul repeat to Samuel?
Saul insisted that he had obeyed, but that the people brought back the best of the plunder to sacrifice to Yahweh at Gilgal.
What was Samuel’s response to Saul?
Samuel said that to obey is better than sacrifice, and that rebellion is as the sin of divination, and because Saul rejected Yahweh’s word, Yahweh rejected him as king.
What reason did Saul give Samuel for his sin?
Saul said he had disobeyed Yahweh’s command because he was afraid of the people, and so he listened to their voice.
What declaration did Samuel give to Saul from Yahweh?
Samuel said that Yahweh had rejected Saul from being king over Israel because Saul had rejected the word of Yahweh.
To whom was Yahweh going to give the kingdom of Israel?
Samuel told Saul that Yahweh was going to give the kingdom to one of Saul’s neighbors, an Israelite who was a better man than Saul.
What did Samuel do to finish the task that Saul had not done?
Samuel hacked King Agag to pieces before Yahweh.
Why did Yahweh tell Samuel to stop mourning for Saul?
Yahweh told him to stop because he had rejected Saul from being king over Israel.
What did Samuel fear would happen if Saul heard he was going to Bethlehem?
He feared that Saul would kill him.
How did Yahweh say that Samuel would know whom to anoint?
Yahweh told Samuel that he would show him what to do and that Samuel should anoint the one Yahweh told him to anoint.
How did the elders of Bethlehem act when Samuel arrived?
They came trembling to meet him and asked if his coming was in peace.
What did Samuel think when he looked at Eliab?
He thought that surely Yahweh’s anointed one was standing before him.
How did Yahweh explain that he does not see as a human sees?
Yahweh said that a human looks on the outward appearance, but Yahweh looks on the heart.
What did Samuel say to Jesse after seven of his sons passed before him?
Samuel said that Yahweh had not chosen any of them.
Where was Jesse’s youngest son before Samuel called for him?
The youngest son was out in the pasture tending the flock of sheep.
What happened to David after Samuel anointed him?
The Spirit of Yahweh rushed upon David from that day forward.
What spirit troubled Saul after the Spirit of Yahweh had turned away from him?
A bad spirit from Yahweh terrified him.
What did Saul’s servants suggest a skillful player on the lyre could do for him?
When the bad spirit was on Saul, the person would play the lyre, and would calm down.
Which of Jesse’s sons did Saul ask to have sent to him?
Saul asked Jesse to send his son David, who was with the flock.
What assignment did Saul give David because he loved him greatly?
What would happen to Saul when David played the lyre?
The bad spirit would turn away from Saul, and he would calm down and feel better.
Why had Saul and the men of Israel encamped in the valley of Elah?
They had drawn up in battle array to fight the Philistines.
What did Goliath have on his head?
He had a helmet of bronze on his head.
What did Goliath carry between his shoulders?
He had a curved sword of bronze between his shoulders.
What did Goliath call the ranks of Israel?
Goliath called them servants of Saul.
What did Goliath say would happen to the Philistines if Israel’s chosen man killed him?
He said the Philistines would become servants to Israel.
When Saul and all Israel heard what the Philistine said, how did they feel?
They lost their courage and became terrified.
Which of Jesse’s sons had followed Saul to the battle?
The three oldest sons of Jesse had followed Saul to the battle.
For how long and how often did the Philistine champion present himself for battle?
He presented himself for forty days, morning and evening.
What was the army doing as David arrived at the camp?
The army was going out to the battle array, shouting the war cry.
As David spoke with his brothers, who came out from the ranks of the Philistines?
As David spoke, the champion, Goliath, the Philistine from Gath, came out from the ranks of the Philistines.
What would the king do for the man who killed Goliath?
The king would enrich the man with great wealth, give him his daughter in marriage, and no longer require that man’s family to pay taxes or do unpaid work for the Israelite kingdom.
What did David say the man who killed the Philistine would take away from Israel?
The man who killed the Philistine would turn away the disgrace from Israel.
What did Eliab accuse David of having in his heart?
Eliab accused David of presumption and evil in his heart, saying David’s motive for coming was to watch the battle.
What did David tell Saul he would do?
David told Saul that he would go and fight with the Philistine.
What did David do to a lion or a bear that took a sheep from the flock?
He went out after it, struck it, and delivered the sheep from its mouth; if it rose against him, he would seize its jaw and strike it and kill it.
Why did David say this uncircumcised Philistine would be like the lion or the bear he had killed?
The Philistine would be like them because he had taunted the arrayed armies of the living God.
Why was David not able to walk in the armor the king provided?
He was not able to walk in the armor because he was not used it.
Why did the Philistine despise David when he saw him?
He despised David because he was only a youth, ruddy, and with a boyish appearance, and Goliath believed he could easily defeat David.
When the Philistine came with a sword, spear, and curved sword, in whose name did David say he came?
David said that he came in the name of Yahweh of Armies, the God of the armies of Israel, whom the Philistine had taunted.
What did David say all the earth would know after he defeated the Philistine?
All the earth would know that the Israelite people worship an all-powerful God.
What did David do when the Philistine drew near to meet him?
David hurried and ran toward the battle line to meet him.
What did the Philistines do when they saw that their warrior was dead?
What did the people of Israel do when they returned from chasing the Philistines?
The people of Israel plundered the Philistine camp.
